note: Checker verdicts for the 2026-11-10 findings (batch 7.5); see docs/audit/README.md

verdicts.title: Focused elements disappear under the sticky Category tabs and the phone Add to order bar (WCAG 2.4.11)
verdicts.problem: When focus moves by keyboard, the browser scrolls the focused control to the screen edge, where the sticky Category tabs (top) or the phone Add to order bar (bottom) cover it completely. Keyboard users lose sight of focus on /menu and while choosing Options on a Menu Item, which fails WCAG 2.4.11 and the docs/05 section 10 promise.
verdicts.fix: In globals.css set scroll-padding on :root when the sticky elements exist, for example ':root:has(nav[aria-label=Categories]) { scroll-padding-top: 5rem }' and, under 48rem, ':root:has([data-sticky-add]) { scroll-padding-bottom: 9rem }'. Add one Playwright check that tabs through the Menu Item at 375 px and Shift+Tabs through /menu at 1280 px and asserts elementFromPoint at the focused element's centre is inside it.
verdicts.reasoning: Code: CategoryTabs is 'sticky top-0 z-10' and the Add bar is 'max-md:sticky max-md:bottom-0 max-md:z-20'; grep finds no scroll-padding or scroll-margin outside three Staff scroll-mt-6 uses. Reproduced on the running build (verify/a11y-1/v1.cjs f1): at 375 Day on /menu/item/hoshi-latte the Sugar '100%' radio (16,696,79x44) and the 'Note for the barista' input (16,742,343x44) are fully covered by the sticky bar; at 1280 Day, Shift+Tab up /menu leaves Ube Latte, Spanish Latte, Hoshi Latte and Kopi Hitam fully covered by the Categories nav. No test covers occlusion (quality.spec's keyboard test runs desktop only and uses .focus()). Next 16.4's route scroll handler already reads scroll-padding-top, so the fix does not fight navigation scrolling. The Cart pill's partial cover only fails AAA 2.4.12, so its scroll-padding is optional.
verdicts.corrections: None of substance. The Cart pill part is not an AA failure (the auditor says so); treat it as optional.

verdicts.title: Cart drawer and phone menu: opening drops or leaves focus outside, Esc loses the place, and Tab runs out behind a full-screen drawer
verdicts.problem: Opening the Cart drawer from the floating pill hides the focused pill (visibility: hidden), so focus falls to <body>: the role=dialog drawer is not announced, and Esc or the next Tab leaves the keyboard user at the top of the page. In both drawers, Tab past the last link walks into page content hidden behind the still-open drawer.
verdicts.fix: Delete the ':root:has(:popover-open) .cart-pill { visibility: hidden }' rule (the top-layer drawer and its backdrop already cover the pill) and add one tiny client leaf that listens for each drawer's toggle event and focuses its Close button when it opens. To stop Tab escaping, either close the popover when focus leaves it or make the Cart a modal <dialog>; add a Playwright check that Enter on the pill moves focus into the drawer and Esc returns it.
verdicts.reasoning: Code: the pill is a popovertarget button; globals.css:227-229 hides it while any popover is open; neither drawer has autofocus or a focus handler. Reproduced (v1.cjs f2, 375 Day, guest Cart storageState): focus on the pill, Enter -> activeElement BODY with the drawer open; Esc -> BODY; Tab -> BODY. Phone menu: Enter on 'Open the menu' keeps focus on the button, now fully covered by the drawer; after 11 in-drawer stops, Tab goes to 'Open in Maps', 'hello@hoshikopi.example', 'Send us an inquiry'... all COVERED while the menu stays open. This is non-modal popover default behaviour, but the Cart drawer claims role=dialog, and the Cart is the core flow.
verdicts.corrections: Do not rely on React's autoFocus prop for the Close button: React only emits the autofocus attribute in server HTML; on client-created nodes (the CartFloat re-renders when the Cart changes) it calls focus() once at mount, while the popover is closed, so later opens would not move focus. A toggle listener is the robust native route. The Invoker Commands <dialog> option needs a support check first. 2.4.11 itself is met (Esc reveals focus), as the auditor notes.

verdicts.title: After a keyboard link or client navigation, focus drops to <body> and the next Tab jumps to the footer (Next 16 Activity keeps the old page hidden in the DOM)
verdicts.problem: After following a link by keyboard, focus is left on the old page's link, which Next 16 now hides with display:none, so focus falls to <body> and the next Tab lands in the footer, skipping the new page. Every client navigation on the site breaks a meaningful focus order for keyboard and screen reader users (WCAG 2.4.3).
verdicts.fix: Add one small client leaf to the (site) layout, inside Suspense, that on a pathname change (not on first load or hash changes) gives the visible main's h1 tabIndex=-1 and focuses it with preventScroll. Add a Playwright check: Enter on a menu card link, then Tab, expects focus inside the new main.
verdicts.reasoning: Next 16.4.3's layout-router says outright: 'This handler intentionally leaves focus untouched; resetting focus on navigation is deferred.' With cacheComponents: true, Activity keeps up to 3 routes in the DOM hidden. Reproduced (v1.cjs f3, 1280 Day): Enter on the Hoshi Latte card -> activeElement BODY, two main#main in the DOM, and the next 4 Tabs go to footer links 'Menu', 'Stars', 'Your account', 'Visit' (not in the visible main). The skip link still works and the route announcer reads the title, so it is not a blocker, but it hits every navigation.
verdicts.corrections: The template.tsx citation is incidental (it only wraps ViewTransition); the cause is Next's Activity plus its focus-neutral scroll handler. usePathname suspends on fallback-param routes (header.tsx comment), so the leaf needs its own Suspense boundary. The duplicate-id labelling side effect was not re-verified and stays low confidence.

verdicts.title: Sign-in and Event Sign-up errors: focus is lost to <body>, and the sign-in error is not announced at all
verdicts.problem: A refused sign-in shows its error only as a described paragraph with no live region, and the disabled-while-pending button drops focus to <body>, so a screen reader user hears nothing and is left at the top of the page. A refused Event Sign-up announces 'Some fields need a fix.' but also leaves focus on <body> instead of the first invalid field.
verdicts.fix: Move the checkout and Inquiry effect (focus the first [aria-invalid=true] after a refusal) into one shared hook and use it in the sign-in and Event Sign-up forms. Focusing the email field also reads its aria-describedby error, so sign-in needs no extra live region.
verdicts.reasoning:
Code: sign-in-form.tsx renders

with no role and no focus handling; signup-form.tsx has role=status but no focus effect; checkout-form.tsx:113-121 and inquiry-form.tsx:27-33 already do the right thing. Reproduced (v1.cjs f4, 375 Day): 'not-an-email' + Enter on 'Email me a link' -> activeElement BODY, and no role=status, role=alert or aria-live in main. Sign-in is the only way into an account, so medium stands.
verdicts.corrections: checkout-form.tsx and inquiry-form.tsx are the pattern to reuse, not defects.

verdicts.title: Submit buttons disabled while pending drop keyboard focus to <body> after successful actions too (Add to order, pairing Add, Cart remove, last Demo step)
verdicts.problem: Buttons that get disabled={pending} lose focus to <body> the moment they are pressed, and Cart remove and the last Demo Mode step unmount the focused button, so focus drops to <body> after the site's most common actions. Tab order survives in Chrome, but screen reader users in browse mode can lose their place.
verdicts.fix: On Add to order and the pairing Add, use aria-disabled with a client-side guard that ignores clicks while pending, instead of the disabled attribute. After a Cart line is removed or the final Demo step runs, move focus to a sensible target (the next line, the Total or the empty-state heading, the status paragraph) with tabIndex=-1.
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced (verify/a11y-1/v2.cjs, a fresh guest Cart of my own, 1280 Day): Enter on Add to order -> BODY during and after 'Added', next Tab reaches 'Save as Favourite' (Chrome keeps the starting point); Remove Kopi Hitam on /cart -> BODY. The status messages are announced, so impact is minor; low stands.
verdicts.corrections: Two mechanisms, not one: Cart remove (and the minus that becomes Remove) and the last Demo step lose focus because the control unmounts; they are plain Server Component forms with no disabled attribute. grep finds 18 disabled={pending...} uses in 16 files, not 13. The recommendation's '(the server already dedupes double taps)' is wrong: lockCart in src/modules/cart/internal/cart.ts only serialises requests, so a second Add adds again, and the client-side pending guard must stay.

verdicts.title: In the Day palette axe cannot check text contrast at all, so the e2e 'both palettes' contrast check only works by Night
verdicts.problem: The Day palette's paper grain is a background-image on <body>, so axe marks almost every text contrast check as incomplete, and the e2e helper fails only on violations. Day text contrast is therefore never enforced in CI, although docs/05 says both palettes pass every check.
verdicts.fix: In expectNoAxeViolations, inject 'body { background-image: none !important }' before analyze() (the tile averages close to the background token), or fail on incomplete color-contrast nodes. Keep the grain in production.
verdicts.reasoning: axe-core 4.14 elementHasImage() returns incomplete 'bgImage' for any element in the background stack with a background-image, which includes body. Reproduced (v1.cjs f6): / at 375 Day gives 145 incomplete and 12 passed color-contrast nodes, reason 'Element's background color could not be determined due to a background image'; the auditor's Night run gives 0 and 157. The e2e suite's openIn Day runs therefore check almost no text contrast.
verdicts.corrections: Severity lowered from medium to low: Day colours pass today (auditor's no-grain run), so this is regression coverage only, with no user impact now. openIn is axe.ts:17-25, not 17-29.

verdicts.title: Placeholder text is 3.16:1 in the Day palette (note field, mobile number, menu search)
verdicts.problem: Placeholders use Tailwind 4's default (the text colour at 50 percent), which is about 3.15:1 on the Day background, below the 4.5:1 that WCAG 1.4.3 asks of placeholder text. It affects the barista note, the checkout mobile number format and the menu search.
verdicts.fix: Add one base rule in globals.css: '::placeholder { color: var(--color-muted-foreground) }' (6.05:1 by Day, 9.34:1 by Night).
verdicts.reasoning: No ::placeholder rule in src; Tailwind preflight sets 'color-mix(in oklab, currentcolor 50%, transparent)'. Runtime (v1.cjs f7): placeholder colour oklab(0.245 ... / 0.5) on rgb(251,246,238); blended #938A81 gives 3.15:1 (my calculation), Night about 4.70:1. axe does not test placeholders.
verdicts.corrections: Severity lowered from medium to low: it is a real AA contrast failure, but every field keeps a visible label and the placeholder is only an example. globals.css:84-88 is the base layer where the rule would go, not the defect.

verdicts.title: Phone header still forces sideways scrolling with larger text, from 125 percent up (UI1-10 not fixed)
verdicts.problem: With a larger default text size (font settings, not zoom), the phone header row does not wrap, so the Cart and menu button are pushed off-screen and every page scrolls sideways. This breaks the docs/05 promise 'Works at 200% text size and 320 px width without horizontal scrolling'.
verdicts.fix: Let the header wrap (flex-wrap), or hide the wordmark text under a header container query while keeping the star and its label. Add one Playwright check with Page.setFontSizes({ standard: 32 }) at 375 px expecting no overflow.
verdicts.reasoning: Code: header is 'flex items-center justify-between gap-4' with no wrap; the 5.2 fix (Cart word sr-only under 360 px) uses a px media query, which text-size changes do not trigger. Reproduced (v1.cjs f8, /menu at 375, empty Cart): scrollWidth 375 at 16 px, 416 at 20 px, 496 at 24 px, 654 at 32 px.
verdicts.corrections: WCAG framing overstated: 1.4.4 and 1.4.10 are met through browser zoom (the auditor's own zoom-equivalent runs show 0 overflow at 320 px, and quality.spec checks 320 px), and the 1.4.12 17 px overflow keeps everything reachable. It is a failure of the design system's own text-size promise and of text-only enlargement, not a strict AA failure, so low rather than medium.

verdicts.title: Not-found and error states keep a generic, wrong or empty page title (WCAG 2.4.2)
verdicts.problem: 404s inside the site keep the default or the page's own title ('Hoshikopi', 'Your order | Hoshikopi'), and a slug that makes the lookup fail renders with no <title> at all. Screen reader users and tab or history lists are not told that the page failed.
verdicts.fix: Return { title: 'Page not found' } from generateMetadata when the slug does not resolve (Menu Item, Event, Post). Render a React <title> in NotFoundBody and ErrorPanel for the cases metadata cannot reach (the Order page, error boundaries), as the Next docs suggest for error boundaries.
verdicts.reasoning: Code: item generateMetadata returns {} when not found; the Order page has static metadata 'Your order' and calls notFound() inside Suspense; nested not-found files cannot export metadata (Next docs: only the root not-found and global-not-found). Reproduced (v1.cjs f9): /menu/item/nope 200 'Hoshikopi', /orders/<zero uuid>?t=x 200 'Your order | Hoshikopi', /events/nope 200 'Hoshikopi', /no-such-page 404 'Page not found | Hoshikopi'. curl of /menu/item/%00x returns the not-found body with no <title> element.
verdicts.corrections: The NUL-slug empty title shares its cause with SEC2-10 (control characters reaching Postgres); fixing SEC2-10 changes that case. Check that a component <title> does not end up next to Next's metadata <title> on the same page.

verdicts.title: Filipino phrases have no lang attribute (WCAG 3.1.2), including the footer line on every page
verdicts.problem: Full Filipino phrases such as 'Salamat sa pagdaan' and 'Magandang umaga' sit in an English page with no lang attribute, so English voices mispronounce them. The site has no lang= anywhere except on the two html elements.
verdicts.fix: Wrap the few full Filipino phrases (footer line, Day hero line, the account greeting where it renders) in <span lang='fil'>. Leave single words such as 'Salamat' alone.
verdicts.reasoning: Code confirms the phrases and the absence of any lang= besides <html lang='en'>. Not in conflict with the dropped 6.5 Filipino batch, which was about translating the site, not marking phrases.
verdicts.corrections: Not a clear 3.1.2 failure: the success criterion exempts phrases that are part of the vernacular of the surrounding text, and the site deliberately writes Filipino-English (CLAUDE.md voice). Mainstream screen readers mostly have no Filipino voice, so the practical gain is small. Lowered to info.

verdicts.title: Checkout contact hint is still not tied to Email or Mobile number (rest of UI1-20)
verdicts.problem: The rule 'One of these is enough: an email or a mobile number' is a loose paragraph between Name and the contact fields, tied to neither input. When both are empty, only Email is marked invalid, though a mobile number alone would also do.
verdicts.fix: Wrap Email and Mobile number in a fieldset whose legend or description carries the rule, or pass it through Field's existing hint prop on both inputs. Mark both inputs invalid with the shared error when neither is given.
verdicts.reasoning:
Code: the

at lines 262-266 has no id and no aria-describedby points to it; Field already supports a hint prop; the zod refine in place.ts puts the error only on path ['customerEmail']. The focus half of UI1-20 is fixed (checkout-form.tsx:113-121).
verdicts.corrections: Impact is softened: the refusal message on Email repeats the either-or rule, so screen reader users do hear it once refused.

verdicts.title: e2e accessibility coverage misses the failure modes axe cannot see; the 38 skips are deliberate project guards
verdicts.problem: The e2e suite has one keyboard test (desktop only, using .focus()) and checks neither focus visibility, focus after drawers, refused forms or navigation, nor larger text. axe never runs on /sign-in, the customer inquiry form, a category page, in-site 404s or error states.
verdicts.fix: Add one small a11y spec: a Tab and Shift+Tab occlusion walk (Menu Item at 375, /menu at 1280), drawer focus-in and Esc return, refused sign-in and Sign-up focusing the invalid field, Page.setFontSizes 32 at 375 with no overflow, and axe on /sign-in, /cafe/inquire, /menu/coffee and an in-site 404. Pair it with the grain fix in axe.ts.
verdicts.reasoning: Verified: quality.spec.ts:80 skips the keyboard test off desktop; no setFontSizes, elementFromPoint or focus-after checks exist in tests/e2e; axe calls follow openIn or flows that never stop on /sign-in or /cafe/inquire (the inquiry test runs axe only on /manage/inquiries). The audit gate log shows 180 passed and 38 skipped, and the skips are project guards.
verdicts.corrections: This is the test side of findings 1 to 8 and can be folded into them in the ranking. gates/e2e.log lives in the audit scratchpad, not the repo.

verdicts.title: Account marketing checkbox is squeezed to 13 px wide by its flex row
verdicts.problem: The marketing consent checkbox has size-5 (20 px) but sits in a flex row without shrink-0, so the long sentence beside it squeezes it to 13 px wide on phones. It renders narrower than every other checkbox.
verdicts.fix: Add shrink-0 to the checkbox, and to the other size-5 checkboxes and radios that sit beside long text in flex rows.
verdicts.reasoning: Measured on the running build as the seeded Member at 375 px (v1.cjs f13): input[name=marketingOptIn] is 13x20. Flex min-width:auto lets a size-5 checkbox shrink to its 13 px intrinsic width. The wrapping label keeps the hit area large, so 2.5.8 passes.
verdicts.corrections: Cosmetic only; lowered from low to info.

verdicts.title: Order Status steps read as 'Placed7:16 AM': no space between the step and its time
verdicts.problem: Each Order Status step renders its label and time as adjacent inline text with only a CSS margin between them. The accessible text runs together as 'Placed7:16 AM'.
verdicts.fix: Add {" "} (or a sr-only ', ') between {step.label} and the time span.
verdicts.reasoning: Code: '{step.label}{step.at && (done || now) && ({formatTime(step.at)})}' with no text node between them; margins do not add whitespace to the accessible text. Not re-run at runtime (it needs an Order), but the code is unambiguous.

verdicts.title: Bar Screen: a new Order arrives with a chime and a slide but no text announcement
verdicts.problem: When a poll brings new Orders, the Bar Screen plays a chime and animates the card but leaves its polite notice region empty. A barista using a screen reader with sound off gets no cue.
verdicts.fix: When arrived.length > 0, also call setNotice with the new Order Codes (for example 'New order K-012'). The aria-live notice already exists and clears itself after 5 seconds.
verdicts.reasoning: Code: poll() only calls chime() and setFresh() for arrivals; setNotice is used only for moves that lost a race and cancels. It fits the product (Staff tools are in scope, one line, native). The realistic user is rare and the visual cue exists, and an arriving Order is not a status message from the user's own action under 4.1.3, so it is a nice-to-have.
verdicts.corrections: Lowered from low to info.

verdicts.title: The public menu crashes when a Category slug has no stand-in icon (Photo looks up ICONS[kind] with no fallback)
verdicts.problem: Photo picks its stand-in icon with ICONS[kind], which holds only the six seeded Category slugs, so any other Category slug renders an undefined component and throws. Every Menu Item has no photo today (ADR 0012), so a Manager who adds a Category with a visible item, or renames a seeded slug, breaks /menu, /menu/[category], the item page and Home.
verdicts.fix: Make Photo total with one fallback, for example 'const Icon = ICONS[kind as PhotoKind] ?? ForkKnifeIcon' with kind typed as string, then drop the five 'as PhotoKind' casts and the two Object.hasOwn guards in /manage/menu. Add one render test with an unknown kind.
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced: rerunning the auditor's renderToString probe with tsx on the real component prints 'coffee OK' and 'smoothies THROWS Error: Element type is invalid ... got: undefined'. The path is real: /manage/menu/categories has a new-Category form with an editable 'Web address' field; saveCategoryAction (requireStaff manager) passes it to saveCategory, whose only slug check is the lowercase-and-dashes regex and max 60, and it creates or updates any such slug. The item editor's Category select lists every Category, so a visible item can be put in the new one. No item has photoUrl in prisma/seed-data.ts and public/menu-concept/ is empty, so every card takes the stand-in path. Public callers cast categorySlug to PhotoKind with no guard, while the two Staff pages already guard. updateTag('menu') after the save means the next render of the menu pages fails at once; (site)/error.tsx catches it, so visitors get the error page instead of the menu. Only the owner holds the Manager role on the demo (Demo Mode gives visitors no /manage), but creating a Category is a supported, unguarded flow and the failure takes out the main public page, so high stands.
verdicts.corrections: Minor: the Staff item page guard falls back to 'coffee', not ForkKnifeIcon (only /manage/menu uses ForkKnifeIcon). A new Category alone does not crash anything; the crash starts once it holds a visible Menu Item without a photo, or at once when a seeded slug is renamed.

verdicts.title: Order Status rules are restated in more than 10 places outside status.ts, and two different definitions of 'the bar's queue' already disagree
verdicts.problem: Pieces of the Order Status table are copied by hand: the bar's next step (customer.ts and bar/actions.ts), the Customer cancel rule, the refundable and cancellable sets, the closed set and the on-the-bar filter each appear two to four times. A change to allowed() can leave a button shown that the server refuses, or hidden when it would be allowed.
verdicts.fix: Export a few pure helpers from ordering next to allowed(): one NEXT map (used by advanceInDemo and bar/actions), isClosed(status), canCustomerCancel(order), and refundable/cancellable predicates that reads.ts and the Order page reuse, plus one shared onBar Prisma where for bar.ts and queue.ts. Keep labels in the UI.
verdicts.reasoning: Each cited copy exists: NEXT in customer.ts:53 and bar/actions.ts:6 are identical; canCancel at orders page:152 restates allowed()'s customer branch; reads.ts:198-207 restates the refund and Manager-cancel sets; ['cancelled','expired','refunded'] appears at orders page:125 and :151, reads.ts:184 and reports.ts:44, 82, 88; bar.ts and queue.ts share the same OR filter. But transition() remains the only writer and re-checks every move, so a drift shows a refused tap with a message, not a wrong Order Status: this is maintainability, not a correctness risk, so low. refund.ts:27-29 must check eligibility before money moves (the provider refund runs before the transition), so a predicate there is reuse, not a second authority. STEP and DEMO_STEP are deliberately different wordings and belong in the UI. The 'two queues disagree' part is a product question already filed: docs/03:132 defines Prep Time as drinks 'in Accepted or Preparing', so windows.ts follows the doc and the gap is DOC-04 / journeys:2, not a code-copy bug.
verdicts.corrections: Severity medium is too high: the server-side table still guards every write. The label maps (bar-screen STEP, orders DEMO_STEP) are UI copy, not rule copies. The Prep Time versus 'drinks ahead' difference matches docs/03:132 and is tracked as DOC-04 and journeys:2; it should be ranked there. The two WAITING constants are a naming clash only (one is a pill tone, one is the drinks-ahead gate).

verdicts.title: Client components copy module rules by hand because index.ts files mix server code with pure rules (no client-safe seam)
verdicts.problem: The Option picker copies the quantity cap (20), the note length (140) and the default-Option algorithm (oneTapOptions), and the Bar Screen re-declares the BarBoard type by hand, fed through an untyped JSON.parse. A rule change on the server will not reach these copies and nothing flags it.
verdicts.fix: Have getMenuItem return the default Option ids from oneTapOptions and pass MAX_LINE_QUANTITY and MAX_NOTE_LENGTH as props from the server page, and type the Bar Screen's data as a small Serialized<BarBoard> (Date to string) imported as a type. Skip server-only and a second rules entry point.
verdicts.reasoning: Verified: option-picker.tsx:16 MAX_QUANTITY = 20 and :172 maxLength={140} copy cart.ts:12-13; initialPicks is oneTapOptions minus the null return; bar-screen.tsx re-declares Order and Board and bar/page.tsx:27 passes JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(...)), which is any. The module index files do import db and next/cache (queries.ts:1-4), so a client value import is not possible today. Impact is small: the server re-checks quantity (addLine refuses too_many) and slices the note to 140, and the server components already use the exported MAX_LINE_QUANTITY (cart page, item actions); only the one client component holds copies. The lazy server-computes-it option is the right shape; 'import server-only' adds a Vitest alias for no current bug.
verdicts.corrections: Severity medium is too high: every copied limit is re-enforced on the server, so drift costs a refused add or a mismatched default, never bad data. Only one client file copies limits; MAX_LINE_QUANTITY is already shared on the server side. The Bar Screen type also describes the /api/bar poll response, so the shared type must cover both.

verdicts.title: Two modules read tables they do not own, and a lib file owns identity's rate_limits table
verdicts.problem: docs/03 says a module touches only its own tables, but ordering reads cafe_settings in placeOrder, cart reads menu's options and menu_items, ordering joins payments, loyalty locks the users row, and rate_limits (filed under identity) is written only by src/lib. Nothing enforces ownership, so the rule in the docs is not what the code does.
verdicts.fix: Add orderCodePrefix to OrderingDay and drop the second cafe_settings read in placeOrder, which also removes one statement from the placement transaction. Then write the sanctioned exceptions into docs/03 section 3 (relation reads for display, the users row lock from ADR 0008, rate_limits owned by src/lib) and re-file rate_limits in docs/04.
verdicts.reasoning: Confirmed by a per-module grep of Prisma delegates and raw SQL: ordering uses tx.cafeSettings (place.ts:271), cart uses db.option (favourites.ts:78), loyalty runs SELECT ... FROM users FOR UPDATE (ledger.ts:38), and only src/lib/rate-limit.ts touches rate_limits. getOrderingDay(at, tx) at place.ts:181 already reads the whole cafe_settings row in the same transaction, so the extra read is pure waste. All of these are reads or locks, nothing breaks, and the users lock is documented in docs/03:140 and ADR 0008. A module-boundary Vitest grep would be heavier than the problem; documenting the exceptions is enough for a portfolio project.
verdicts.corrections: The auditor's 'no other cross-module table access' is wrong: relation includes also cross ownership, cart.ts:117 and favourites.ts:67 read menu_items, and ordering reads.ts:112 and :176 read payments. Severity medium is too high for read-only access with no failure mode today. The module-boundary test in the recommendation is optional at most.

verdicts.title: Results do not follow the ADR 0001 convention ({ ok: false, reason } and { ok: false, errors }), and Server Actions use five different state shapes
verdicts.problem: A few module results break the ADR 0001 shape (enterSecondFactor returns a string, storeMenuPhoto returns { error }, startBusyMode throws on a refusal), and cancelOrder drops refundOrder's result so a failed refund is invisible. The same form-result and form-state types are declared five or more times each.
verdicts.fix: Fix the one behavioural gap under PAY-05 (cancelOrder returns the refund outcome and the callers show it), and declare FormResult and FormState once, for example in src/lib/forms.ts, for the modules and the four /manage action files. Leave the other outliers until they are next touched, or note them in ADR 0001.
verdicts.reasoning: All cited outliers exist: SecondFactorResult = 'ok' | 'wrong' | 'too_many'; PhotoResult uses error; RefundOutcome is a string union; startBusyMode throws 'Busy Mode takes 10 or 15 minutes...'; addLine answers a bad quantity with reason 'invalid_options'; refund.ts:62-70 ignores refundOrder's result. The errors-record type is repeated in edit.ts, save-hours.ts, save-details.ts, content.ts, inquiries.ts, place.ts and signups.ts, and the 'idle' | 'saved' | 'error' state in four action files plus SaveBar. Most outliers are harmless: startBusyMode only receives the fixed button values, so a bad value is tampering and throwing fits 'bugs throw'; RefundOutcome is an internal payments-to-ordering contract; void writes with no refusal path are fine. The only user-facing harm is the dropped refund result, already filed as PAY-05.
verdicts.corrections: ADR 0001 covers module results only, so the five Server Action state shapes are variety, not an ADR breach. Severity medium is too high; the real impact is PAY-05's and should be ranked there. startBusyMode's throw is defensible under the ADR's 'bugs throw' clause. Converting every outlier is more churn than value before Phase 9.

verdicts.title: Validation is not 'zod at the edge' as docs/03 section 13 says: Zod lives in modules, actions check by hand, and the Zod helpers are copied 2 to 8 times
verdicts.problem: docs/03:162 says every input is parsed with Zod at the edge, but Zod runs inside the modules while Server Actions read FormData by hand. The issue-to-errors loop is copied 8 times, the P2002 check 3 times and the text() helper 3 times, and email is checked with z.email() on two forms and a hand regex on three.
verdicts.fix: Change docs/03:162 to say modules parse their input with Zod and Server Actions only read FormData. Add one fieldErrors(error) helper (a line over z.flattenError, Zod 4.6 is installed) for the 8 copies, and use z.email() everywhere instead of the regex.
verdicts.reasoning: Verified counts: 'errors[String(issue.path[0])] ??= issue.message' in exactly 8 module files; 'const text = (form, name)' in 3 action files; P2002 checks in edit.ts, content.ts and signups.ts; z.email() at place.ts:146 and save-details.ts:24 versus /^[^\s@]+@[^\s@]+\.[^\s@]+$/ in sign-in actions, signups.ts and inquiries.ts. Validation in modules is the better seam (it is what Vitest exercises), so the doc is what is wrong, not the code. The duplication is a few lines per copy; the email rules differ only on edge inputs. The unvalidated writes named in the evidence are real but small and already filed (adjustStars has no upper bound, staff:11; pauseOrdering is clamped in its action).
verdicts.corrections: Two email rules, not three (one regex copied three times, plus z.email()). The slug maxima differ by entity (Menu slugs 60, content slugs 80), which reads as deliberate rather than drift. Severity medium is too high for helper duplication plus a stale doc line; the doc part is the same drift as architecture:23. A full shared helper set (email, slug, checkbox, hhmm, isUniqueClash, Object.fromEntries everywhere) is more than the problem needs.

verdicts.title: /manage/cafe hand-rolls Field, SaveBar, Panel and fieldClass, and its three Markdown fields lack the MarkdownField preview
verdicts.problem: The cafe details form re-implements fieldClass, Field, SaveBar and a fieldset panel instead of using the shared components the other six /manage forms use. Its three Markdown fields (directions, the space, the story) are plain textareas, while Event and Post bodies get MarkdownField's live preview.
verdicts.fix: Use Field for the inputs, MarkdownField for directionsMd, spaceMd and storyMd, and SaveBar with a children slot for the 'See the Visit page' link. Keep the local fieldset panel unless Panel gains a fieldset variant, since Panel renders a section with a heading.
verdicts.reasoning: Verified line by line: cafe-form.tsx:34 is fieldClass character for character; text() and area() repeat Field's label, hint, aria-invalid, aria-describedby and error; the submit block repeats SaveBar's button and role=status line; MarkdownField is used only in content-forms.tsx; SaveBar is used by exactly six /manage forms. /cafe renders all three fields through Markdown (cafe/page.tsx:191, 212, 295), so the missing preview is a real Manager gap, and the spaceMd hint does not even say it is Markdown. The hand-rolled copy's ARIA wiring is correct today, so this is duplication and a small UX gap, not an a11y bug.
verdicts.corrections: Severity medium is too high: nothing is broken and the copy's ARIA is right. Panel is a section with an h2/h3, not a fieldset, so 'use Panel' would change form semantics; the local fieldset helper is fine. About 90 lines is right.

verdicts.title: Field's children mode is a leaky interface: custom selects and inputs must wire ids and ARIA by hand, and two public forms lose the link to their error
verdicts.problem: When Field gets children it renders them untouched, so its hint and error ids and aria-invalid reach only its own input; the selects in the inquiry, Event Sign-up and Menu Item forms show an error that is not tied to the control. Textareas cannot use Field at all, so the inquiry message block is rebuilt by hand.
verdicts.fix: Let Field take a render function for children that receives { id, name, 'aria-invalid', 'aria-describedby' }, and use it in the four select and input callers. Textareas can then use the same path.
verdicts.reasoning: Confirmed: fields.tsx:35 renders '{children ?? <input ... aria-describedby={describedBy} />}', so children get none of it; inquiry-form.tsx:62 and signup-form.tsx:96 pass error to Field around a bare select; stars-form.tsx wires aria by hand and comments why. Realistic a11y impact is small: these selects offer only valid fixed values, so their field error appears only for a tampered request, and a seat shortage comes back as the form-level message (too_many_seats), not errors.seats. The interface leak is real and cheap to fix, which is why it is worth doing, but the 'two public forms lose their error' harm is mostly theoretical.
verdicts.corrections: One more caller has the same gap: item-form.tsx:76 (Category select with error). Severity medium is too high because the select errors are effectively unreachable in normal use; the checkout contact hint (a11y:11, UI1-20) is the user-facing instance.

verdicts.title: Business workflows live in Server Actions instead of modules (Event Sign-up limits and auto-confirm, account deletion, inquiries, adding a Favourite)
verdicts.problem: Account deletion runs five module calls in sequence with no transaction, so a failure part way leaves some data behind. The Event Sign-up per-visitor limit, its undo, the Member auto-confirm and the link format live in the Server Action, outside the module seam Vitest tests.
verdicts.fix: Give deidentifyOrders, forgetStars, deleteMemberCart and forgetMember an optional client and run them in one db.$transaction from the action (identity cannot import the others without a cycle). Move the Sign-up limit, auto-confirm, link and notify call into content's signUpForEvent taking a visitor key and member email, so tests:14 can cover it.
verdicts.reasoning: Verified: deleteAccountAction calls deidentifyOrders, forgetStars, deleteMemberCart, signOut and forgetMember in turn with no transaction; signUpAction holds PER_VISITOR = 2, takeToken then cancelSignup, the member-email confirm and the '${site}/events/${slug}/signup/${id}?t=${token}' link. The deletion gap is real (ID2-08). The Sign-up move is useful mainly for testability (tests:14). The inquiry action is only a rate limit plus a best-effort email after the save, which is reasonable edge work, and addFavouriteAction pricing at most a Member's few Favourites to find one is negligible.
verdicts.corrections: The inquiry and Favourite parts add little and can be dropped. A failed deletion is recoverable (signing in again and deleting again), so the impact is low. The signup action still needs the request IP from headers, so the action must pass a visitor key; it cannot all move.

verdicts.title: Authorization is split: some modules enforce the Manager role, others trust the caller, and three different actor shapes exist
verdicts.problem: Most Manager-only module writes trust their caller to have run requireStaff('manager'), while refundOrder and adjustStars also check the role themselves, and adjustStars types its actor loosely. A future caller that skipped requireStaff would not be stopped by the module.
verdicts.fix: Keep role checks at the edge as ADR 0005 and docs/03:159 decide, and keep covering them with the Server Action access tests already filed (tests:13). Optionally type adjustStars' actor as identity's Staff, a one-line change.
verdicts.reasoning: The split is a recorded decision, not drift: ADR 0005 and docs/03:159 say requireStaff(role) guards pages, Server Actions and route handlers, and edit.ts:9-10 and save-hours.ts:8-9 state 'Callers check the role'. The Second Factor (ADR 0014) can only be enforced by requireStaff at the edge, so module-level role checks would duplicate the role half and still miss the 2FA half. The auditor and staff:23 both confirmed every /manage action calls requireStaff with the right role today. The three actor shapes serve different needs (ordering's Actor includes customer, webhook, system and demo; audit only needs an id). The risk named is hypothetical and is exactly what tests:13 would catch.
verdicts.corrections: Not a defect: it follows ADR 0005 and docs/03:159. Moving role checks into modules would contradict that decision and needs a new ADR. The only small, real nit is adjustStars' loose actor type, which overlaps architecture:20.

verdicts.title: The 8.10 shared components are not used everywhere: raw h1 headers, hand-rolled panels, 8 copies of a large primary pill, 3 stat tiles, 5 saved notices
verdicts.problem: The large primary submit pill (min-h-12 px-6) is pasted as a class string in about eight places beside the shared PRIMARY_PILL (min-h-11 px-5), so the same role has two heights. Stat tiles and the 'See it on the site' saved notice are each hand-built three to five times, and a few pages hand-roll their h1.
verdicts.fix: Add one PRIMARY_PILL_LG constant next to PRIMARY_PILL and use it in SaveBar and the forms. Leave the stat tiles, saved notices and headers until those pages are next touched.
verdicts.reasoning: Counts mostly hold: the exact large-pill string is in 5 files (fields.tsx SaveBar, inquiry, signup, sign-in, cafe), with variants in second-factor-form, hours/page.tsx and the stars-form override; Stat and Tile are near-identical and reports inlines a third; the saved notice appears on 5 editor pages with slightly different classes; PageHeader is used in 29 files. This is visual consistency polish with no user-facing defect, so low value before Phase 9 apart from the one-constant pill fix.
verdicts.corrections: role-form.tsx:10 is a copy of the regular min-h-11 px-5 pill, not the large one. manage/page.tsx:144 is a Suspense fallback heading. The saved notices are near-copies with differing classes, not identical. Item, Event and Post detail pages hand-roll their h1 inside a hero layout on purpose.

verdicts.title: The Concept Notice (a CLAUDE.md rule) is pasted in 5 places with no component, while a one-line PickupLine has one
verdicts.problem: The Concept Notice sentence and its /concept link, which CLAUDE.md requires on every page and at checkout, is pasted into five files with slightly different classes. A wording or link change must be made five times, and a new frame has no component to reach for.
verdicts.fix: Add a ConceptNotice component in src/components with a className prop (and a plain <a> option for global-error.tsx) and use it in the five places. The e2e check can then target one test id.
verdicts.reasoning: Verified: the identical text 'Hoshikopi is a concept cafe. Orders and payments here are for demonstration. About this concept' appears in checkout/page.tsx, bar/layout.tsx, global-error.tsx (with <a>), manage/layout.tsx and footer.tsx, and nowhere as a component, while PickupLine wraps one sentence and is used 12 times. The other 'concept cafe' lines (Events, privacy, /dev/pay, inquiry) are page-specific copy, not the Notice. Small, cheap and in line with the CLAUDE.md rule.

verdicts.title: Each page view prices the Cart twice: the header button and the floating Cart each call getCart (three times on /cart)
verdicts.problem: Every customer page renders CartButton in the header and CartFloat in the (site) layout, and each calls getCart(owner), which is not cached per request, so the Cart is read and priced twice per view. /cart and /checkout price it a third time, and CartFloat still does its work there although HiddenOn then hides it in the browser.
verdicts.fix: Add `export const currentCart = cache(async () => { const owner = await currentCartOwner(); return owner ? getCart(owner) : null; })` in cart/internal/session.ts, export it from cart/index.ts, and use it in CartButton, CartFloat and the Cart page. Caching currentUser (ID1-16) and a units field on CartView are optional extras.
verdicts.reasoning: Traced: currentCartOwner is wrapped in React cache() (session.ts:24) but getCart (cart.ts:107) is a plain async function that runs cart.findUnique with nested includes and then priceChoices' menuItem.findMany with nested includes. Prisma has no relationJoins preview feature here (generated client previewFeatures: []), so each getCart is several SQL statements. Both callers sit in separate Suspense boundaries of the same RSC request, so cache() dedupes them. No other cache layer exists (the only cache( in src is session.ts:24). On /checkout the third call is checkoutView (reads.ts:49), on /cart it is the page's Cart() (page.tsx:76).
verdicts.corrections: The duplicate is one extra getCart per view (two Prisma calls, several SQL statements each without relationJoins), not just 'two extra queries'. The third read on /checkout comes from ordering's checkoutView, which takes the owner as an argument; leave it alone and dedupe only the two shell components plus the Cart page.

verdicts.title: clock.ts lacks day-string helpers, so date conversions and the Sold Out rule are hand-rolled 3 to 10 times each
verdicts.problem: The 'is this Sold Out today' rule is written three times in the menu module (queries.ts:79, staff-queries.ts:6, pricing.ts:73), and Date-to-Manila-day and day-to-Date conversions are hand-rolled in about 10 and 4 places even though clock.ts already has dayValue(). Formatting a Manila day uses two idioms (a T04:00:00Z Date in 4 places, manilaInstant(day, 12 * 60) in 3).
verdicts.fix: Export one isSoldOutToday(soldOutOn, today) from menu/internal/pricing.ts and use it in queries.ts and staff-queries.ts; add dayOf(date) and formatDay(day) to clock.ts and use them plus the existing dayValue() at the copied sites. Leave the weekday and month arrays (short, long, plural and months, partly in client forms) and the 'last N days' helper unless those files change anyway.
verdicts.reasoning: Recounted by grep: `T00:00:00Z` outside clock.ts at reads.ts:173, details.ts:83-84 and hours.ts:56,61; `toISOString().slice(0, 10)` 10 times outside clock.ts and hours.ts (manage/menu/item/[id]/page.tsx:42,120, details.ts:99, ordering-day-db.ts:91, inquiries.ts:94, pricing.ts:31,73, queries.ts:80,91, staff-queries.ts:7); `T04:00:00Z` 4 times; manilaInstant noon 3 times; windowStart/starTotals/reports page share the `addDays(today, 1 - days)` boundary; 6 name arrays (hours-list.tsx:4, cafe/page.tsx:91, weekly-form.tsx:14, hours-forms.tsx:17, weekly-list.tsx:5, account/page.tsx:71). The three Sold Out copies agree today (all compare the UTC date string of soldOutOn with manila(now()).day), so this is drift risk, not a bug. The proposed six new clock helpers are more than the risk needs; the Sold Out helper is the part with real value because menu, Staff page and pricing must agree.
verdicts.corrections: Counts hold. hours-list.tsx:4 is a sixth name array not in the locations. The full helper set (addMinutes, startOfLastDays, weekdayName via Intl) is optional polish; the smallest useful change is one Sold Out helper plus dayOf/formatDay, so effort is S rather than M.

verdicts.title: Money is still formatted and summed outside money.ts in a few places, and the Order page's receipt does not use the receipt format
verdicts.problem: The Event page's JSON-LD formats money as `((event.priceCents ?? 0) / 100).toFixed(2)` outside money.ts, which breaks the CLAUDE.md rule 'format only through src/lib/money.ts'. Staff forms reuse formatReceipt as a serialiser, so a field labelled 'Base Price (PHP)' starts as 'PHP 185.00'.
verdicts.fix: Add toDecimal(cents) to money.ts ('1250.00': no grouping, no 'PHP') with a unit test, and use it for the JSON-LD price and the four form defaults. Leave the raw reduce sums and the Order page as they are.
verdicts.reasoning: events/[slug]/page.tsx:83 confirmed and it is the only toFixed or `/ 100` outside money.ts (grep). It is exact for integer centavos, so it is a rule breach, not a wrong number; ADR 0002 says 'only lib/money.ts formats money for people', and JSON-LD is machine-read, but CLAUDE.md states the rule without that exception. formatReceipt as a form default confirmed (item page 100 and 108, options page 132, events page 87); parsePesos accepts 'PHP 185.00', so it works, it just reads oddly. The addMoney point does not hold: the three raw sums (reads.ts:210, reports.ts:55, manage/orders/page.tsx:170) add Int columns read from Postgres, which cannot be non-integers, while addMoney guards price composition (cart.ts:149, pricing.ts:142). The receipt point is weak: roadmap 2.6 defines the receipt as the Order placed email (with its VAT part), which already uses formatReceipt and vatPart (templates.ts:37,52); neither ADR 0002 nor docs/03 says the Order status page is a receipt.
verdicts.corrections: Covers the earlier checker's toFixed(2) break. The 'addMoney applied inconsistently' and 'Order page receipt disagrees with ADR 0002' parts are not real issues (integer DB sums; the receipt is the email per roadmap 2.6). Missed: manage/events/[id]/page.tsx:87 and manage/menu/item/[id]/page.tsx:108 also use formatReceipt as form defaults, and place.ts:77 (baseOf) is another raw integer sum.

verdicts.title: A Server Action reads Date.now() directly (outside clock.ts), and Order history and Star rows still take the database clock
verdicts.problem: addToCartAction returns `{ status: "added", at: Date.now() }`, a server-side wall-clock read outside clock.ts that CLAUDE.md forbids; the value is only the key that restarts the 'Added' animation (option-picker.tsx:233). Order events and the earn, reserve, release, reverse and adjust Star entries still take Prisma's @default(now()) instead of lib/clock, while placedAt and the Birthday Treat use now().
verdicts.fix: Make the nonce a counter from the previous state, `at: (_prev.status === "added" ? _prev.at : 0) + 1`, which needs no clock (now().getTime() would repeat under freezeClock). Pass `at: now()` and `createdAt: now()` in transition(), placeOrder's first Order event and the ledger writers, as DATA-14 proposes.
verdicts.reasoning: grep for Date.now()/new Date() outside clock.ts finds only this server read plus the browser-side status-poller.tsx:103-104 and the theme script (ADR 0010), so the earlier checker's break is exactly this line. status.ts:177-186 creates orderEvent with no `at`; ledger.ts:49-56 and the other starEntry.create calls pass no createdAt except the Birthday Treat (ledger.ts:204 `createdAt: at`); place.ts:294 sets placedAt from now() but its nested 'placed' event at 296-301 has no `at`. schema.prisma gives order_events.at and star_entries.created_at @default(now()). Effect is only under freezeClock (tests, demos), as DATA-14 says.
verdicts.corrections: The default timestamp comes from Prisma's @default(now()) (the wall clock of Prisma or Postgres), not specifically the database clock; same effect. The 'placed' event inside placeOrder is another unclocked write the finding does not list.

verdicts.title: Business constants and keys are restated as literals: '9 Stars', '15 drinks', '30 minutes', 20 Favourites, allergen and badge keys in 3 places each, 'Kapitolyo, Pasig' in 9
verdicts.problem: Exported rules (STARS_PER_REWARD, MAX_DRINKS_PER_ORDER, HOLD_MINUTES, MAX_FAVOURITES) are restated as literals in customer copy, and allergen and badge keys are listed three times each. The menu's dietary filter (menu-card.tsx:20-24) matches display labels such as 'Vegan' and 'Contains nuts', so renaming a label silently breaks the filter.
verdicts.fix: Give MenuItemCard badge keys (or ready filter tags) so the filter reads keys, and keep one allergen table and one badge table in a client-safe menu file used by edit.ts's enum, allergens.ts, fields.tsx and the Staff form. Interpolate the constants where copy is server-rendered, pass them as props to the client forms, and use cafe.area only in the Event JSON-LD, the Event calendar file and the email footer.
verdicts.reasoning: All literal counts verified by grep: '9 Stars' at checkout-form.tsx:155,332, checkout/actions.ts:53, account/page.tsx:173; '15 drinks' at inquire/page.tsx:20,30,47 and inquiry-form.tsx:70; HOLD_MINUTES imported nowhere and '30 minutes' in 6 copy strings; MAX_FAVOURITES unexported; ALLERGEN_KEYS, NAMES and ALLERGEN_LABELS; BADGE_KEYS, queries BADGES (4 public labels) and item-form BADGES (6). events/[slug]/page.tsx loads getCafeDetails and shows cafe.area at line 157 but hard-codes 'Kapitolyo, Pasig' in its JSON-LD at 77. Counter-evidence: most literal sites are client components (checkout-form, inquiry-form, signup-form, signup-answer, item-form all start with 'use client') that cannot import a module's index.ts, so interpolation needs props or a client-safe file (architecture:3). Several 'Kapitolyo' strings are deliberate brand copy that cannot read the database without turning prerendered metadata dynamic: root layout metadata, the OG image alt and tagline, and /concept, which explains that Kapitolyo is real but Hoshikopi is not there.
verdicts.corrections: Of the 9 'Kapitolyo, Pasig' copies only 3 should follow cafe.area (Event JSON-LD, calendar.ts, the email footer); the root metadata, OG image, page descriptions and /concept text are static brand copy. Many literals live in client components, so 'interpolate the exported constants' needs a client-safe seam or props. notify cannot import content's HOLD_MINUTES (notify depends on nothing), so it must be passed in.

verdicts.title: Oversized files: three page functions of about 335 to 350 lines carry domain logic that should be split or moved
verdicts.problem: bar-screen.tsx (559 lines), account/page.tsx (554) and orders/[id]/page.tsx (477) each hold one very long function, which makes them slow to review. The Order page also decides Order Status questions (closed, canCancel, onBar, live) inline.
verdicts.fix: Split only when a feature next touches these files: BarScreen into client sub-components in the same client tree (ManagerControls, Lane, Card) and Account into its three Panels. Move the Order page's status predicates into ordering as part of architecture:2, not as a separate refactor.
verdicts.reasoning: Line counts reproduced exactly with wc -l (the top 11 files match the finding). BarScreen's four Manager forms show or hide on the polled board.paused and board.busy and call poll() after submit (bar-screen.tsx:293-370), so they must stay inside the client tree; 'server-rendered ManagerControls' is the wrong shape, and the 'ships Manager forms as client code' impact is negligible (four small forms). The Order page predicates (page.tsx:151-163) are already listed in architecture:2's locations. The Account split is a readability change with no defect behind it, and the files are not wrong, only long; little value before Phase 9.
verdicts.corrections: The Bar Screen's Manager controls depend on polled client state and cannot be server-rendered without losing that; split them as client components instead. The Order page predicate move duplicates architecture:2. Severity lowered to info: no defect, readability only.

verdicts.title: Dead and test-only exports: HOLD_MINUTES and SignupView are exported but never imported, about 10 index exports serve only tests, and about 45 file-local symbols are exported
verdicts.problem: content/index.ts exports HOLD_MINUTES, which nothing outside the module imports, and several index exports (mergeGuestCart, readEvents, readPosts, readRecurringEvents, nextOrderCode, popularDrinks, fakeProvider) exist only for tests without saying so. busyAction repeats startBusyMode's BUSY_MINUTES and BUSY_FOR_MINUTES check so it can return quietly where the module throws.
verdicts.fix: Use HOLD_MINUTES in the Sign-up copy (with the constants finding) instead of deleting it, and add a one-line '/** Tests only */' comment on each test seam in index.ts. Leave the `export` keywords inside internal/ and SignupView as they are.
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced exports.txt by grep: HOLD_MINUTES and SignupView have no importer outside content; the listed seams are imported only by tests/db/*. Tests must go through index.ts because the boundary rule blocks internal/ imports from tests (boundary probe: CAUGHT for tests/), so test seams on index are deliberate. Actor, PlaceOrderInput and ProviderEvent are the parameter types of public functions (transition, placeOrder, the provider interface), and SignupView is the return type of signupForGuest, so they belong on the interface. The ~45 file-local exports under internal/ are invisible outside their module (lint blocks internal imports), so removing `export` changes no interface; tsc --noUnusedLocals --noUnusedParameters reports 0 errors (tsc-unused.txt is empty). BUSY_*: confirmed; busyAction (actions.ts:117-129) repeats the check, and bar-screen.tsx:347-350 hard-codes the same [10, 30] and [15, 60] pairs as a third copy. Making busyAction rely on startBusyMode needs startBusyMode to return a refusal instead of throwing (architecture:5).
verdicts.corrections: SignupView is not dead (it names an exported function's result), and Actor, PlaceOrderInput and ProviderEvent are not test-only in spirit. The 57 'dead' internal exports include notify's three templates (used by notify/index.ts) and freezeClock/unfreezeClock (intentional test seams). Removing internal `export` keywords does not narrow any module interface, so that part adds nothing. Severity lowered to info.

verdicts.title: Type safety at the edges: stringly typed statuses and Payment Methods, four casts of the Order Line options snapshot, and the Bar Screen's untyped initial data
verdicts.problem: The Order Line options snapshot (a Json column) is read back with four hand casts, and Payment Method, Payment status and Star kind travel as string with Record<string, string> label maps, so a new enum value compiles with a missing label. The Bar Screen's initial board is JSON.parse output (any), unchecked against the client's Board type.
verdicts.fix: Add one snapshotOptions(json) reader in ordering and use it at the four sites, and type the label maps and view fields with the generated enums (Record<OrderStatus, string>, Record<PaymentMethod, string>, Record<StarKind, string>). Leave the Bar Screen typing to architecture:3's Serialized<BarBoard>.
verdicts.reasoning: grep 'options as' finds exactly bar.ts:101, emails.ts:27, reads.ts:142 and reads.ts:249. schema.prisma has OrderStatus, PaymentMethod, PaymentStatus and StarKind enums, and src/generated/prisma/enums.ts is a plain constants file ('You can import this file directly'), so client and shared components can use the types. OrderView.status already uses OrderStatus while paymentMethod (reads.ts:78) and payment.status (reads.ts:94) are string; ORDER_STATUS_LABEL and OrderStatusPill take string; PAYMENT and KIND are Record<string, string>. bar/page.tsx:27 passes JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(...)). tsc-index.txt (noUncheckedIndexedAccess) has 74 errors on about 40 lines in src, mostly benign. No runtime bug today; it is compile-time safety for future enum changes.
verdicts.corrections: The noUncheckedIndexedAccess figure is 74 errors on about 40 src lines (151 including tests), not 45 sites; immaterial.

verdicts.title: Site URL, auth secret and token hashing are re-implemented in 4 to 7 places with different fallbacks
verdicts.problem: `process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL ?? "http://localhost:3000"` is repeated in 7 files, so a production deploy missing the variable sends localhost links in emails and JSON-LD. BETTER_AUTH_SECRET is read in 4 files with 3 different fallbacks (throw, empty string, 'local').
verdicts.fix: Fold this into ops:5's src/lib/env.ts: one siteUrl() and one authSecret() that throw when unset in production, used at the 7 and 4 call sites, plus orderPath(id) in links.ts so reads.ts:166 stops stripping the origin with a regex. Skip a shared tokens.ts: the sha256 helpers are one-liners and payments/sign.ts implements the provider's signature scheme, not an app token.
verdicts.reasoning: Counts verified by grep: 7 site-URL fallbacks, BETTER_AUTH_SECRET read in links.ts:8 and signups.ts:22 (throw), second-factor.ts:20 (?? "") and provider.ts:47 (?? "local"), hashing in links.ts, signups.ts, cart/session.ts and payments/sign.ts. The fail-open risk for the secret is overstated: Better Auth throws at startup in production when the secret is missing (node_modules/better-auth/dist/context/create-context.mjs: 'You are using the default secret...' throws when isProduction), and provider.ts:36-38 also throws in production without it, so the empty TOTP key and 'local' fallbacks are reachable only in development and tests. The real fail-open is the localhost site URL, which ops:5 already covers.
verdicts.corrections: Different secret fallbacks are not a production risk because Better Auth refuses to start without the secret in production. The hashing helpers serve different purposes (payments/sign.ts is the provider webhook signature), so a shared tokens.ts is not worth it; the env helpers are the useful part and overlap ops:5.

verdicts.title: notify mixes inline templates in index.ts with templates.ts, and every caller outside ordering wraps sends in its own try/catch
verdicts.problem: notify/index.ts holds the sign-in, Inquiry and Event Sign-up email texts inline, while the Order emails live in templates.ts with unit tests. The Inquiry and Sign-up actions each wrap their send in their own try/catch and console.error.
verdicts.fix: Move the Inquiry and Sign-up texts into templates.ts and add cases to templates.test.ts when those emails next change. Put ops:6's timeout in outbox.send(), which every email already passes through, and keep the callers' try/catch, since sign-in must tell the user when the link was not sent.

A zero-code alternative (the owner widens Opening Hours on the live demo in /manage/hours) works but makes the invented cafe read as open 24 hours on /cafe and hides the ORD-07 closed state from everyone.

verdicts.title: After a failed online payment there is no retry: the Cart is gone, the message repeats, and the Order holds its window for 15 minutes
verdicts.problem: After a failed online payment the Order page repeats 'didn't go through' twice, tells the Customer to 'place it again' although the Cart was emptied at placement, and offers no way to pay again. The Order keeps its Pickup Window (and any reserved Stars) until the 15-minute sweep unless the Customer finds the Cancel button.

Drop the duplicated sentence and point the text at the Cancel button, or cancel the failed Order at once and refill the Cart from its Lines as Order again already does for Members.

A 'Cancel order' button is on the failed page (canCancel is true for placed; run.log line 162 shows it), so the window and Stars can be freed at once, and Members get 'Order again', which rebuilds the Cart. More importantly, with PayMongo the failed state is unreachable: parseEvent takes the payment.failed resource id (pay_...) as checkoutId, which never matches a cs_ checkout (interim PAY-06), and PayMongo's hosted checkout lets the payer retry in the same session, so 'Finish paying' stays. In practice this is a demo-only dead end reached by pressing 'Make the payment fail'.
verdicts.corrections: 'Its only button was See the menu' is wrong: Cancel order is shown (and Order again for Members). 'Holds its window for 15 minutes' only applies if the Customer does not cancel. The real-life 'declined GCash or card' impact does not arise with PayMongo today because failed events never match (PAY-06). Severity medium -> low.

(last-order-note.tsx:28-30): coherent, but it gives no reopening time. After 9:00 PM, OpenStatus does say "Closed now, opens 7:00 AM tomorrow", so the gap covers 30 minutes a day.

verdicts.title: When another tab changes the Cart, checkout says "Prices changed"
verdicts.problem: If another tab changes the Cart, Place order compares only the total and answers "Prices changed: your total is now PHP 260", although no price changed. If the other tab's change leaves the total the same, the Order is placed with Lines this tab never showed.
verdicts.fix: Send a fingerprint of the rendered Cart (sorted Line ids and quantities) with seenTotalCents, and return a distinct cart_changed reason when it differs. Word it as "Your Cart changed in another tab: it's now PHP 260. Check it and place your order again."
verdicts.reasoning: placeOrder computes the total and returns price_changed whenever it differs from input.seenTotalCents (place.ts:203-206). No other check compares the rendered Lines with the current ones. messageFor maps price_changed to the "Prices changed" text (actions.ts:46-47). An emptied Cart is caught earlier as cart_problem (place.ts:193-195), which matches the reviewer's j10 result. The server still charges exactly what it reprices, so no money is at risk (ORD-06 holds). Only the wording, and the rare equal-total case, are wrong.
verdicts.corrections: Additional case not in the finding: an edit in another tab that keeps the same total passes the check silently.

verdicts.title: A wrong or truncated Order link shows a generic "This page could not be found" with HTTP 200 and no way to recover
verdicts.problem: A wrong, truncated or token-less Order link shows the generic "This page could not be found" page, still titled "Your order", with links only to the menu and Home. It says nothing about using the full email link or signing in to see Your orders.
verdicts.fix: Add src/app/(site)/orders/[id]/not-found.tsx with Order-specific copy, such as "We couldn't open this order. Use the full link from your email, or sign in to see Your orders.", and a sign-in link back to /account#orders. Leave the 200 status alone: Next 16 sets it for streamed pages.

The stale "Your order" title belongs with a11y:9, and the /dev/pay 200 belongs with PAY-12. Members can already recover through /account#orders; phone-only Guests are covered by journeys:8.

verdicts.title: Demo Mode lets any Member mint Stars and records unpaid Pay at Pickup Orders as counter sales
verdicts.problem: In Demo Mode a visitor's own taps take a Pay at Pickup Order to Picked Up, which marks it paid at the counter, earns its Stars and counts it in the Manager's sales report. ADR 0015 records these side effects as intended.
verdicts.fix: No change needed for the demo. If the owner wants clean demo reports, add one note on /manage/reports while demoMode() is on ("Includes Orders visitors moved in Demo Mode") rather than changing transition() or the Star rules.
verdicts.reasoning: The mechanics are as described. isBar admits the demo actor while demoMode() is on (status.ts:36-37). changes() sets paidAtCounter and paidAt for Pay at Pickup on picked_up (status.ts:90-93), earnForOrder runs (status.ts:164-173), and salesReport counts every picked_up Order (reports.ts:31). ADR 0015 says: "Side effects stay the same: the Ready email, Pay at Pickup marked paid at the counter, Stars earned." Demo Mode runs only with the fake provider, so Stars have no value (ADR 0006). The Stars a visitor mints land only on their own Star Card. /manage/reports needs a Manager with a Second Factor, which a live-demo reviewer cannot get (ID1-03 and FEAT-01: only the owner signs in as Staff). Excluding demo Orders from reports or leaving paidAtCounter false would contradict the ADR and make the demo's Picked Up step behave differently from a real one. The stated benefit is small.
verdicts.corrections: "The reports a reviewer may open" does not hold: live-demo reviewers cannot open /manage/reports. Member Pay at Pickup Orders are capped only by the 15-drink limit, checkout rate limits and Capacity, not by the Guest limit; this does not change the verdict.

verdicts.problem: Home never mentions Demo Mode or the "Try it in two minutes" guide, and the guide always says "sign in with Google first", even where Google sign-in is not configured. Handle the Barista picks label under UI2-24 and the Guest Stars idea under FEAT-07, which needs an ADR amending ADR 0005 because Guests earn no Stars by design.

The sign-in page shows Google only when googleEnabled() is true (sign-in/page.tsx:98). barista-picks.tsx:66-72 is a Link labelled "Add to order", the same issue as UI1-21 and UI2-24. The Guest panel says "Collect Stars next time" (page.tsx:468-471), the same issue as FEAT-07. ADR 0005 states Guests earn no Stars, so attaching a Guest Order to a new Member needs its own ADR and test-first Stars work. The missed live-demo sign-in email is journeys:9.
