verdicts.title: The fake checkout's "Cancel and go back" doesn't cancel, and the page then says "We got your order"
verdicts.problem: The Test Mode checkout's "Cancel and go back" link only returns to the Order page. The Order stays Placed, still holding its Pickup Window and any reserved Stars until the Customer cancels or it expires after 15 minutes.
verdicts.fix: Rename the link to "Go back without paying". The fake then matches PayMongo, where cancel_url is the same Order page and cancels nothing, and the Order page already offers Finish paying and Cancel order.
verdicts.reasoning: dev/pay/[id]/page.tsx:76-81 is a plain Link to the Order page with no action. The Order page then shows the accurate Placed message "Finish paying to send it to the bar." (page.tsx:85), with Finish paying and Cancel order buttons. The real adapter sends success_url and cancel_url as the same return URL (paymongo.ts:48-49), so cancelling on the real provider does not cancel the Order either. Changing the fake to cancel would make the demo behave differently from production. The defect is the label, not the flow. Holding Capacity for up to 15 minutes is the designed unpaid-Order rule (ADR 0007).
verdicts.corrections: Of the two recommendations, keep only the relabel. Making the fake link cancel the Order would diverge from PayMongo's cancel_url behaviour.

verdicts.title: Menu search and dietary filters: accents don't match, 'Nut-free' lists merchandise, and 'No caffeine' hides all food
verdicts.problem: The Nut-free filter is computed from the absence of a nut allergen, so the Tumbler and the bagged beans count as nut-free menu items. Vegan and No caffeine are opt-in badges, so the three filters mean different things. Search also does not fold accents, so "café" finds nothing although Cafe Mocha exists.
verdicts.fix: Derive dietary tags only for food and drinks (skip the beans-and-merch Category, or tag only items whose Category is food or drink). Label the caffeine filter as drinks-only ("Caffeine-free drinks"). Normalise both the query and data-search with normalize("NFD").replace(/\p{Diacritic}/gu, "").
verdicts.reasoning: menu-card.tsx:20-24 sets nut-free when badges lack "Contains nuts", and badges come from allergens (queries.ts:70-75). Seeded merch has no allergens, so the Tumbler and House Blend get nut-free (run.log line 26 lists the tags). vegan and no-caffeine come from badges that only some drinks carry (seed: Calamansi Honey Soda and Tanglad Ginger Tea are no_caffeine). Search matches with includes() on lowercased text without accent folding (menu-filter.tsx:19-26). All three claims hold. Hiding food under "No caffeine" is defensible, because caffeine is a drink property; the real issue is the mixed opt-out and opt-in semantics. The accent miss is narrow: no seeded name has an accent, and "café" is about the only natural case.
verdicts.corrections: "No caffeine hides all food" is better read as a labelling choice than a defect. The core inconsistency is that nut-free is opt-out while vegan and no caffeine are opt-in.

verdicts.title: Once the bar marks an Order Ready, the Customer's page checks only every 30 s, and in Demo Mode still offers 'Hand it over' after the bar has done it
verdicts.problem: After Ready, the Order page polls every 30 seconds, so a collected Order can still read Ready for up to 30 seconds. That interval is the cadence ADR 0009 sets.
verdicts.fix: No change needed. If faster follow-up after Ready is wanted, lower the Ready gap to 10 to 15 seconds in status-poller.tsx and update ADR 0009 and docs/03 section 7 in the same change.
verdicts.reasoning: status-poller.tsx:101-102 uses 30_000 ms while status is ready. ADR 0009 line 8 and docs/03-ARCHITECTURE.md:148 both specify "then every 30 seconds", so this is a recorded decision. The "refused silently" part does not hold. demoAdvanceAction calls refresh() whatever advanceInDemo returns (actions.ts:19-27), and advanceInDemo refuses a stale from-status (customer.ts:76-78). A tap on the stale "Hand it over" therefore re-renders the page as Picked Up ("Enjoy! See you again soon.") and the panel disappears. A visibilitychange also triggers an immediate check. The stale-button case needs Staff and a demo visitor acting on the same Order, which happens only locally or when the owner uses the Bar Screen on the demo.
verdicts.corrections: The 30-second gap after Ready is documented in ADR 0009, not an inconsistency. A refused demo tap is not silent: the page refreshes to the current status.

verdicts.title: The reduced-motion rule gives every element a 0.01 ms 'all' transition, so a Day/Night flip under reduced motion costs about 1 to 3 s of style work on a phone
verdicts.problem: The reduced-motion block sets transition-duration: 0.01ms !important on every element, and because transition-property defaults to all, every colour change on a Day/Night flip starts a real CSS transition. Under reduced motion one flip creates 650 to 900 transitions and costs 1 to 3 s of style recalculation on a throttled phone, about ten times the cost with motion on.
verdicts.fix: In the reduce block use transition-duration: 0s !important (or transition: none !important) and keep 0.01 ms only for animation-duration. With that override the flip creates no transitions and costs the same as with motion on.
verdicts.reasoning: Read globals.css:282-292: the rule targets *, ::before, ::after, ::backdrop with transition-duration 0.01ms, and the initial transition-property is all. Re-measured with my own script (verify/motion-1/flip.cjs) on the :3300 build: 375 px at 4x CPU, / gave 851 to 855 transitions and 998 to 3036 ms RecalcStyle per flip under reduce vs 0 transitions and 49 to 91 ms with motion; /menu 645 transitions, 1155 to 1221 ms vs 109 to 124 ms. At 1280 unthrottled: 697 to 907 transitions, 132 to 233 ms vs 5 to 16 ms. Injecting transition-duration: 0s !important under reduce brought it back to 0 transitions and 49 to 109 ms (375) and 8 to 14 ms (1280). grep finds no transitionend or animationend listener in src, so the 0.01 ms value buys nothing. The trigger is rare (the header switch and the 6 AM / 6 PM flip), but the freeze is long when it happens and lands on the audience the rule is meant to protect, so medium stands.
verdicts.corrections: Measured cost per flip at 375/4x on / was 1.0 to 3.0 s (the audit said 1.3 to 1.5 s); same conclusion.

verdicts.title: Under reduced motion, Add to order shows no visible confirmation on phones: the 'Added' overlay ends invisible and everything else is off screen
verdicts.problem: The 'Added' overlay on the Add to order button uses the confirm keyframes, which end at opacity 0, and the reduced-motion rule jumps every animation straight to its last frame, so reduced-motion users never see it. On a phone the sticky Add to order bar is in use, the status line sits below it off screen, the header is not sticky and the Cart pill is hidden on Menu Item pages, so nothing visible says the drink was added.
verdicts.fix: Give reduced-motion users a static 'Added' for 1.6 s, either with a state flag and timer that swaps the label or with an opacity-only hold keyframe re-enabled for .animate-confirm inside the reduce block. Add one Playwright check at 375 under reduce that 'Added' is visible on the button after the add.
verdicts.reasoning: Code path holds: option-picker.tsx:231-240 renders the span with animate-confirm (confirm 1600ms both); @keyframes confirm (globals.css:182) ends at opacity 0; the reduce block forces animation-duration 0.01ms !important, so fill both lands it on opacity 0 at once. The status line is outside the sticky [data-sticky-add] div, header.tsx's header is static (no sticky or fixed), and globals.css:231-235 hides .cart-pill below 48rem when [data-sticky-add] exists. The auditor's screenshot add-375-reduce-1.png shows only 'Add to order' on the button after the add. The e2e suite asserts the role=status text, never the visible button label, so it passes. docs/05 section 7 promises the final state, and here the final state is hidden. A sighted reduced-motion phone user can easily add a drink twice, which they only notice in the Cart.

verdicts.title: The page fade leaves the new page unclickable for about 0.35 s after it appears; the CSS comment says clicks pass through
verdicts.problem: The whole page is one named view-transition participant, and while the fade runs the browser skips named participants when hit-testing, so taps on the new page are dropped until the fade ends (about 330 ms after the new content commits; the header and footer stay clickable). The comment at globals.css:268-269 says clicks pass through to the live page, which is true only for the unnamed header and footer.
verdicts.fix: Remove the 80 ms delay on ::view-transition-new(.page) and shorten the rise so the non-clickable window is roughly halved. Correct the comment to say the header and footer stay clickable while the page itself does not until the fade ends.
verdicts.reasoning: The Next guide (view-transitions.md:362-370) states that hit-testing skips named participants for the transition's duration even with ::view-transition { pointer-events: none }. My own probe (verify/motion-1/hit.cjs, 1280, motion on) found the new h1 in the DOM from about 170 ms after the click but elementFromPoint returned BODY until 516 ms, when the last view-transition animation ended; the header link stayed hit-testable throughout. Under reduce the window was about 40 ms. The core claim and the wrong comment hold. The impact is overstated: the window coincides with the new page being invisible for 80 ms and then still fading in, and a deliberate tap on content that has not yet appeared is rare, so it is a polish issue, not a medium bug.
verdicts.corrections: Downgraded from medium to low. The '0.4 s later settle' is the cost of the page fade the owner asked for in 8.9 (docs/05 specifies 120 ms out and 250 ms in), not a defect; only the 80 ms delay is undocumented. The dropped-tap window after the new content commits is about 330 ms at 1280, not the 0.35 to 0.45 s from the click the title implies. The root-only crossfade idea would also fade the header and footer on every navigation, so it is a trade-off, not a free fix.

verdicts.title: On Home the Star Card lights its Stars on page load, 3.5 to 5.5 screens below the fold, so the delight is over before anyone can see it
verdicts.problem: The Star Card's Stars and lines animate on the document timeline with 50 ms staggered delays, so they finish within about 550 ms of page load. On Home the card sits after the hero, Barista picks, Popular and the whole printed menu, so the promised delight is over long before anyone scrolls to it.
verdicts.fix: On Home, drive the Star Card's animations from a view timeline (animation-timeline: view() with staggered animation-range values) inside the existing @supports and no-preference guards. Or keep the lit card on Home and change the docs/05 row to say the moment plays on the account pages only.
verdicts.reasoning: star-card.tsx uses animate-pop and animate-fade-in with animationDelay index x 50 ms, no scroll timeline. page.tsx renders StarsAndNews after Hero, two BaristaPicks, PopularThisWeek and PrintedMenu, so the card is several screens down at any width (the auditor measured y=4489 at 375 and y=2839 at 1280). On /account and /account/stars the card is near the top, so the moment works there. The .reveal scroll-driven pattern already exists in globals.css, so the CSS-only fix fits ADR 0011.

verdicts.title: Bar Screen: a new card accepted within 4 s slides in again in the Making lane, and one shared 4 s timer cuts a later arrival's gold edge short
verdicts.problem: When a barista accepts a new Order within 4 s of its arrival, the card remounts in the Making lane while its id is still in fresh, so it slides in again with the gold edge as if it were new. Each arrival replaces the fresh set and starts its own 4 s timer that clears the whole set, so a later arrival can lose its gold edge after about 1 s and an earlier one loses it as soon as the next arrives.
verdicts.fix: Apply animate-arrive and the gold edge only in the New lane and drop an id from fresh when it is tapped. Keep an arrival time per id (or one timer per id) so every arrival keeps its full 4 s.
verdicts.reasoning: bar-screen.tsx:160-161 does setFresh(new Set(arrived ids)) then setTimeout(() => setFresh(new Set()), 4000), a replace plus a clear-all. card() is called per column (lines 428 and 436), so an Order that moves from New to Making mounts a new Card under a different parent and the animate-arrive class (line 472) restarts the keyframe. advance() awaits poll() right after the Server Action, so the move happens immediately after the tap, well within 4 s when the barista is quick. Low: it is a misleading visual cue, not a lost Order.
verdicts.corrections: The card() helper is at lines 211-221 (the audit cited 212-216). The replace also cuts the earlier arrival's highlight short, not only the later one's.

verdicts.title: The Bar Screen makes a new AudioContext for every chime and never closes it
verdicts.problem: chime() on the Bar Screen creates a new AudioContext for every new Order and every unmute and never closes it, so a tablet left on the board accumulates one live audio context per arrival over a shift. The Order page's chime already reuses one module-level context.
verdicts.fix: Copy the status-poller.tsx pattern: one module-level AudioContext created on first use (the mute toggle is a tap that unlocks it), resumed when suspended and reused for every chime.
verdicts.reasoning: bar-screen.tsx:80 runs new AudioContext() inside chime(), called from poll() (159) and toggleSound() (230), with no close(). status-poller.tsx:9 and :24 use let audio and audio ??= new AudioContext(). A running AudioContext is not garbage collected until closed in Chromium, which the auditor's ac.cjs showed (200 running contexts). Safari's behaviour is unconfirmed (Playwright WebKit on Windows has no AudioContext; I saw typeof AudioContext === 'undefined' there too). Real cost is battery and CPU on a long shift; low.

verdicts.title: The Cart count does not bump on the first Add to order where it can be seen, and 'goes up' is measured against the count at page load
verdicts.problem: CartCount bumps only when the count is above the value it had when it first mounted, and the floating Cart pill mounts only once the Cart holds something, so the pill appears without motion on the first add while the header count bumps off screen (the header is not sticky). Because the baseline is the first value, the header count also fails to bump on an increase after items were removed, and it bumps on a decrease that stays above the first value.
verdicts.fix: Compare with the previous count instead of the first one (a ref updated after render, or the previous-render pattern in save-details-button.tsx) so the bump plays only on an increase. Give .cart-pill an @starting-style entrance (opacity and translate, 250 ms, ease-calm) so its first appearance moves too.
verdicts.reasoning: cart-count.tsx:16 keeps useState(count) as onLoad and line 20 applies animate-bump when count > onLoad, with key={count} restarting the span on every change. cart-float.tsx:20 returns null for an empty Cart and HiddenOn unmounts the pill on /cart and /checkout, so its CartCount always starts at the current count. cart-button.tsx:23-24 says the header keeps an empty CartCount deliberately so the first add bumps, but header.tsx has no sticky or fixed position, so on a Menu Item page the bump is usually off screen. The decrease case follows from the same code: load with an empty Cart, add 3, remove one on /cart, and the header count (2 > 0, new key) bumps.
verdicts.corrections: Addition: the same baseline also makes the header count bump when the count goes down (for example removing a Line on /cart) while it stays above the page-load value, against docs/05's 'when it goes up'.

verdicts.title: No page fade between /account and /account/stars, or between an Event and its Sign-up page
verdicts.problem: A template remounts only when its own child segment changes, and account/ and events/[slug]/ have no template.tsx, so /account and /account/stars swap instantly, as does the Sign-up page's link back to its Event. Every other customer page change fades, against docs/05's 'Every customer page'.
verdicts.fix: Add src/app/(site)/account/template.tsx and src/app/(site)/events/[slug]/template.tsx, each re-exporting the (site) template like menu/template.tsx does. Or list the exceptions in docs/05 section 7.
verdicts.reasoning: find shows templates only in (site), cafe, events, menu, menu/item and news. For /account to /account/stars the (site) template's child segment stays 'account', and for /events/x/signup/y to /events/x the events template's child segment stays '[slug]=x', so neither remounts and no enter/exit fires. account/page.tsx:208 links to /account/stars and stars/page.tsx:88 links back, so this is a common path. The auditor's nofade.cjs counted 0 startViewTransition calls for both account directions.
verdicts.corrections: The Event direction is reversed: the Sign-up page is reached from the emailed link (a full page load, which never fades anyway) because signup-form.tsx shows its result inline; the in-app navigation without a fade is the Sign-up page's Back link and 'Back to the Event' pill to /events/[slug].

verdicts.title: The automatic switch at 6 AM and 6 PM flips the palette instantly, while the manual switch crossfades
verdicts.problem: The per-minute clock check in THEME_SCRIPT writes data-theme directly, so an open page in Auto mode jumps from the cream Day palette to the navy Night palette in one frame at 18:00 and back at 06:00. Only the manual header switch wraps the change in a View Transition crossfade.
verdicts.fix: In the setInterval tick only, when the chosen palette differs from the current one and the page is visible, apply it inside document.startViewTransition where available; leave the first, before-paint call and the function exposed to the header switch as they are. Fix finding 1 first, since this flip also runs under the reduced-motion transition rule.
verdicts.reasoning: theme.ts:13 pick() sets d.dataset.theme=c and runs from setInterval(pick,60000); theme-choices.tsx:34 is the only startViewTransition call. ADR 0010 says the page flips at 6:00 and 18:00 while open but says nothing about how, so a crossfade does not conflict with it, and it matches 8.9's 'every state change moves a little'. Value is small (an open page at the exact minute), hence low.
verdicts.corrections: Do not put the View Transition inside pick() itself: choose('auto') already calls window.hoshikopiTheme() inside its own startViewTransition, and a nested call would skip the outer transition. Wrap only the interval tick.

verdicts.title: docs/05 section 7 has drifted from the code: stale Pickup chips line, 'View Transitions are skipped', 'ease-calm for everything', and the page fade's delay
verdicts.problem: docs/05 section 7 still says the Pickup Time chips wait for batch 8.3 (done 2026-11-08), that View Transitions are skipped under reduced motion (they still run, only without animation), that --ease-calm is used for everything, and that the new page simply fades in over 250 ms. The code uses the UA default for the theme crossfade, Tailwind's default easing for the FAQ plus and the menu-view ring, ease-in for the old-page fade, and an 80 ms delay before the new page.
verdicts.fix: Update section 7: delete the chips sentence, say View Transitions run without animation under reduced motion, and mention or remove the 80 ms delay. Either give the stray transitions --ease-calm (for example a --default-transition-timing-function override) or relax the 'for everything' wording.
verdicts.reasoning: Line 195 ends 'until batch 8.3 replaces them' and roadmap line 170 marks 8.3 done. Line 197 says 'View Transitions are skipped'; globals.css:293-297 sets only animation: none on the pseudos and my hit probe saw a 40 ms non-hit-testable window under reduce, so the transition still runs. globals.css has no ::view-transition-*(root) rule and no --default-transition-timing-function override; cafe/page.tsx:279 and printed-menu.tsx:127 use bare transition-transform; globals.css:274 uses ease-in. globals.css:278 adds animation-delay: 80ms, absent from line 185.
verdicts.corrections: Also the old-page fade uses ease-in (globals.css:274), another exception to 'ease-calm for everything'.

verdicts.title: The drawers slide out only in Chromium; Firefox and Safari close them at once (graceful, but docs/05 says they slide back out)
verdicts.problem: The drawer's close animation depends on transitioning the overlay property, which only Chromium supports, so in Firefox and Safari the phone menu and Cart drawer vanish at once on close. docs/05 says they slide back out without that caveat.
verdicts.fix: Add 'slides back out where the browser supports overlay (Chromium); elsewhere it closes at once' to the Phone menu row in docs/05 section 7. No code change.
