Function is unaffected; only the doc claim needs a caveat.

verdicts.title: No browser test runs with motion on, so none of the motion bugs above can be caught
verdicts.problem: playwright.config.ts sets reducedMotion: 'reduce' for every test and nothing in tests/ overrides it, so no test ever runs with motion on. The Add to order tests assert only the role=status text, so the invisible 'Added' under reduce and the dropped taps during the page fade pass the suite.
verdicts.fix: Add one small motion.spec.ts that sets reducedMotion: 'no-preference' and checks that a tap right after a menu-card navigation lands and that the Bar Screen arrive plays once. Under reduce at 375, assert that 'Added' is visible on the button after Add to order.
verdicts.reasoning: playwright.config.ts:21 sets reducedMotion: 'reduce' under use; grep for reducedMotion, emulateMedia and prefers-reduced in tests/ finds nothing else. cart.spec.ts, menu.spec.ts, bar.spec.ts and order.ts check getByRole('status') toContainText('Added'), never the button overlay. UI2-28 asked for one reduced-motion check once motion landed; 8.9 instead switched the whole suite to reduce, which is right for axe but leaves motion untested.

verdicts.title: No error monitoring or alerting: money-related failures exist only as console lines that Vercel Hobby keeps for 1 hour
verdicts.problem: Failures that need a person, above all a late payment whose automatic refund throws, are only written with console.error, and Vercel Hobby keeps runtime logs for 1 hour with no alerts. The late-paid Order then sits Expired or Cancelled with a paid Payment that no Manager screen lists and that refundOrder refuses to refund.
verdicts.fix: List Orders whose Payment is paid while the Order is Expired or Cancelled with no Refund row on /manage/orders, and let refundOrder accept them, so the 'refund by hand' case becomes a button. Add onRequestError in src/instrumentation.ts that prints one structured line, and if an uptime check is wanted, ping a DB-touching route no more than hourly.
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced: no src/instrumentation.ts; webhook.ts:66 logs 'refund by hand' and still answers 200, so PayMongo never retries; refund.ts:29-30 makes only picked_up (Manager) or cancelled-with-paidAt eligible, and a late payment never sets paidAt because the paid transition failed, so no UI path exists. Roadmap 7.2 promises a late payment is 'refunded or shown to the Manager, never dropped'; the 'shown' half is missing on the failure branch. Vercel's runtime logs page (fetched 2026-11-13) confirms 'Hobby | 1 hour of logs'. grep of docs/ finds no monitoring, alerting or uptime text. On the live demo the fake provider's refund is a database update and practically cannot fail, so today this is dormant, but the product is built as if real and the gap is a money path.
verdicts.corrections: Fix step (3) as written would hurt on Neon Free: a typical 5-minute uptime check on a route running SELECT 1 keeps the compute awake around the clock (scale to zero needs 5 idle minutes), about 180 CU-hours a month at 0.25 CU against the 100 CU-hours Free allows (Neon plans page, fetched 2026-11-13). Ping hourly or less, or check a route that does not touch the database. Step (1) also needs refundOrder's eligibility widened, not only a list. A third-party tracker such as Sentry is optional for a Hobby demo; a structured console line plus the Manager list covers the money case.

verdicts.title: No backup or restore plan for the production database, and Production builds migrate it with no snapshot first
verdicts.problem: Production builds run prisma migrate deploy on Neon with no snapshot, and no doc says how to restore the database or that Neon Free keeps only 6 hours of history. A bad migration or a mistaken SQL edit noticed after 6 hours cannot be undone.
verdicts.fix: Add a 'Backups and restore' line to docs/06-SETUP.md section 9: create a Neon branch of production before merging a pull request with a migration, and note where restore lives and its 6-hour window on Free. A paid Neon plan belongs on the 'Becoming real' list.
verdicts.reasoning: vercel.json:3 confirmed. grep for backup, restore, point-in-time, pg_dump and snapshot in docs/ (outside docs/audit) finds only ADR 0014's 'No backup codes'. Neon's plans page (fetched 2026-11-13) says Free instant restore is 'up to 6 hours, limited to 1 GB of change history per project'. The core claim holds. Severity is lower for this product: the live data is seed data plus test Orders, all in Test Mode with no real money (ADR 0006), and the seed can rebuild the menu; the cost is a lost demo, not lost sales.
verdicts.corrections: Severity medium to low for the Hobby demo. The weekly pg_dump to the owner's drive is optional and more than a demo needs; the Neon branch before a migration is the one step worth writing down.

verdicts.title: Migrations land before the new code and outlive a rollback, with no rule that they stay compatible with the running deployment
verdicts.problem: The new schema goes live before next build and stays if the build fails or the deployment is rolled back, and nothing says migrations must keep working with the previous release. A future drop or rename would break the live site for the length of a build, or until a forward fix after a rollback.
verdicts.fix: Write the rule into docs/06-SETUP.md section 9 and CLAUDE.md: add first, drop or rename only in a later release once no code reads the column, and fix forward rather than roll back past a migration. Keep migrate deploy before next build.
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced: vercel.json:3 migrates then builds; Vercel Instant Rollback swaps code only; no doc mentions expand, backward compatibility or rollback. The signup_confirmation example holds: the migration back-fills only existing rows, and heldSignups (signups.ts:15-19) drops an unconfirmed Sign-up after 30 minutes, so a Sign-up taken by the old code during the build window would lose its Seats. That window is a minute or two on a demo with almost no traffic, and all 14 migrations so far are additive, so the impact is theoretical today.
verdicts.corrections: The optional fix (run migrate deploy after next build) is wrong for this app. With Cache Components, next build prerenders 'use cache' reads (menu/queries.ts, cafe/details.ts, content/content.ts and others) against the production database, so a build whose code selects a new column would fail against the old schema; migrating first is what lets additive releases build at all. Severity medium to low.

verdicts.title: No CI and no dependency update bot: quality gates run only when someone remembers, and advisories are found by hand
verdicts.problem: The public repository has no GitHub Actions workflow, no dependabot.yml and no Renovate config, so lint, tests and npm audit run only through a manual npm run qa. A pull request can be merged and deployed to production, migrations included, without any check, and security releases surface only when someone looks.
verdicts.fix: Add one .github/workflows/ci.yml on pull_request with a Postgres service that runs lint, format:check, typecheck, Vitest against a _test database and npm audit --omit=dev, and require it on main. Add a grouped weekly .github/dependabot.yml for npm and github-actions.
verdicts.reasoning: Confirmed: no .github folder, no renovate config; package.json qa and qa:full are the only gates; Next 16's next build type-checks but no longer lints. The better-auth lag (ID1-17, SEC1-11, fixed in 7.3) shows advisories were found by audit, not by a bot. Product fit is good: green checks are visible on a public portfolio repository and GitHub Actions minutes are free for public repositories. The roadmap's definition of done does make the batch agent run npm run qa before each pull request, which lowers the 'merge red' risk, but nothing enforces it.
verdicts.corrections: Minutes are not a reason to keep Playwright off pull requests (public repositories run free); the real reasons are the wall-clock and shared-state flakiness in tests:4 and tests:7. Dependabot alerts and security updates can also be switched on in the repository settings without a file; I could not read those settings (gh is not signed in here). The qa scripts are at package.json:16-17, not 17-18.

verdicts.title: Environment variables are never validated at startup; several fail open to localhost, an empty key or the Resend test sender
verdicts.problem: Seven places fall back to http://localhost:3000 when NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL is missing, so a misconfigured production build would send localhost links in emails, calendar files and share cards. The payment provider's own checks run only at the first checkout, after the Order is committed, so a bad provider setting shows up as failed checkouts rather than a failed deploy.
verdicts.fix: Read the site address through one helper that throws in production when NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL is unset, and replace the seven fallbacks with it. In next.config.ts, when VERCEL_ENV is production, call providerFor(process.env) and check the few required variables so a misconfigured deploy fails its build.
verdicts.reasoning: The localhost fallbacks are real (grep finds seven, not six), and NEXT_PUBLIC_ values are inlined at build, so a missing one is baked in. providerFor (provider.ts) fails closed but lazily, and place.ts:333-336 logs and returns payment_start_failed after the commit. Several listed 'fail open' cases do not hold in production, though, which makes this low rather than medium: the variables are set on the live deploy and every misconfiguration shows at the first request.
verdicts.corrections: BETTER_AUTH_SECRET: Better Auth itself throws in production when the secret is missing (node_modules/better-auth/dist/context/create-context.mjs validateSecret, isProduction = NODE_ENV production), and links.ts and signups.ts throw too, so a Second Factor cannot be encrypted with the empty key in production; the '' fallback in second-factor.ts:20 is a dev-only smell (ID1-12). CRON_SECRET missing gives 401, which is a deliberate fail-closed, and expiry also runs on read (docs/03 section 12). MAIL_FROM's fallback is Resend's test sender, the documented choice until a domain exists (setup section 9 step 2). A zod env schema is fine but more than needed; one site-URL helper plus a production check in next.config.ts covers the real cases.

verdicts.title: Emails are sent inline with no timeout or retry: a slow Resend would stall Bar Screen taps, webhook replies and checkout
verdicts.problem: The Resend fetch has no timeout and is awaited in the request path of the Bar Screen's Ready tap, the payment webhook, Pay at Pickup checkout and refunds, so a slow Resend would hold those responses. When Resend refuses an email only the status code is logged, not Resend's reason.
verdicts.fix: Add signal: AbortSignal.timeout(5000) to the Resend fetch and include await response.text() in the error. Leave after() and retries until Resend is actually turned on with a domain.
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced: outbox.ts:20 fetches with no signal; transition() awaits emailOrderReady and emailOrderPlaced after commit (status.ts:131-132); webhook.ts:58, place.ts:321 and refund.ts:48 await emails; attempt() in emails.ts catches errors but cannot cut a hang short; outbox.ts:34 keeps only response.status. Mitigations: the email runs after the transaction commits, so no row lock is held while it waits; undici's connect timeout is 10 s, so only a slow response (not an unreachable host) can stall for long; and RESEND_API_KEY is unset on the demo (roadmap 5.4: Resend skipped until a domain exists), so the code path is dormant.
verdicts.corrections: Kind is a robustness gap, not a bug: nothing misbehaves today. Severity medium to low because it is dormant and Resend slowdowns of minutes are rare. Moving emails into after() needs care: transition() sends them itself and also runs in Vitest, outside a request scope where after() throws, so the timeout alone is the lazy and sufficient fix. Sign-in link emails go through the same send() and benefit from the same timeout.

verdicts.title: The image optimizer accepts any party's Vercel Blob store under /menu/, so anyone can spend the Hobby image-transformation quota
verdicts.problem: images.remotePatterns allows *.public.blob.vercel-storage.com under /menu/, which matches every Vercel Blob store, so anyone can push their own images through hoshikopi.vercel.app/_next/image. Each new source and width costs one of the 5,000 monthly Hobby transformations, and once they are gone new images answer 402 until the month resets.
verdicts.fix: Replace the wildcard with this store's own host, <store-id>.public.blob.vercel-storage.com, taken from the first real upload's URL. Re-run the probe: a made-up store under /menu/ should then answer 400.
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced on 2026-11-13: /_next/image?url=https://verifyfakestore123.public.blob.vercel-storage.com/menu/x.jpg&w=640&q=75 gave 404 NOT_FOUND (accepted, fetched upstream), while the same host under /other/ gave 400 INVALID_IMAGE_OPTIMIZE_REQUEST. Vercel's image limits page (fetched 2026-11-13) gives Hobby 5K transformations a month and says that beyond it 'New images will fail to optimize and instead return a runtime error response with 402 status code' while cached images keep working, and a changelog title says exceeding it no longer pauses deployments. The one-line fix is right.
verdicts.corrections: Severity medium to low. Today no image goes through the optimizer at all: public/menu is empty, the stand-in panels are not images (ADR 0012), and roadmap 5.4 says the first real upload has not happened, so exhausting the quota breaks nothing visible. The enforcement question the auditor left open is answered: new images fail with 402 and show alt text; the project is not paused. Motivation for an attacker against a portfolio demo is low.

verdicts.title: Still present on the live demo: seeded Event, Promo and seasonal dates are running out (Latte art night is already past)
verdicts.problem: The seed dates its Events, Promo and seasonal drink from the day it ran and cannot be re-run, so on the live demo Latte art night is already past, the only upcoming Event is Nov 21, and the Promo ends Dec 1. The Event Sign-up flow (EVT-02, protected in 8.7) cannot be shown on the live site at all, because the remaining Event has no Seats.
verdicts.fix: Before the Phase 9 review, have the Manager add one or two Events with Seats dated well ahead in /manage/events and push the Promo and seasonal end dates in /manage/menu; no code is needed. Only if this keeps recurring, add a Demo Mode-only refresh, not logic in the production cron.
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced live on 2026-11-13: /events lists 'Past Events Latte art night Sat, Nov 7'; Home's 'Upcoming event' is 'Open mic under the stars, Sat, Nov 21'; /menu/item/matcha-latte shows 'Promo until Tue, Dec 1'. seed-data.ts sets evening(7) and evening(21) and dayFromNow(30) and dayFromNow(60); seed.ts refuses a second run. The demo is the portfolio's product, and Phase 9 (measure, case study, rehearsed demo script) comes after these dates, so medium stands.
verdicts.corrections: The Sign-up flow is not lost 'from Nov 22': it went on Nov 8, because only Latte art night has seats (12) and Open mic has none ('Sign up at the counter on the night'). The Tapa Rice Bowl pairing does not point at an off-menu item: the pairing read filters by inSeasonWhere (src/modules/menu/internal/queries.ts:290-292), so the 'Goes well with' card simply disappears. Rolling seeded rows forward in /api/cron/daily puts demo-only logic in production code; the Manager tools already cover it, so effort is S, not M.

verdicts.title: The daily cron does no housekeeping: rate-limit keys (emails and IPs), guest Carts and expired verifications pile up
verdicts.problem: Nothing deletes old rate_limits rows, whose keys hold emails and IP addresses, or abandoned guest Carts, so both grow without a retention rule. The setup doc says the cron runs at 6:00 AM Manila, but Hobby fires it anywhere in that hour.
verdicts.fix: Add two idempotent deletes to /api/cron/daily: rate_limits with window_start older than 2 days (the longest window is 1 day) and guest Carts not updated for 30 days, the cookie's maxAge. Change the doc wording to 'between 6:00 and 6:59 AM Manila'.
verdicts.reasoning: Confirmed: the cron does only expireUnpaid and revalidateTag; grep finds no delete of rate_limits or guest carts in src. The longest takeToken window is 86,400 s (events actions.ts:67), so a 2-day cutoff is safe. Vercel's cron page (fetched 2026-11-13) gives Hobby 'Per-hour (±59 min)'; the seeded opening is 7:00 AM, so only the wording is off. Growth at demo traffic is tiny against Neon's 0.5 GB, so the value is mostly the personal-data retention (DATA-09), and low is right.
verdicts.corrections: Expired verifications are already handled: Better Auth deletes every verification with expiresAt in the past on each findVerificationValue (node_modules/better-auth/dist/db/internal-adapter.mjs:802-806), that is on every sign-in link check, so that delete is not needed. docs/03 section 12 says 'before opening', not '6:00 AM'; the exact-time wording is in docs/06 section 9 (line 130) and roadmap 5.4.

verdicts.title: The function region (sin1) lives only in the Vercel dashboard; vercel.json and the setup checklist do not pin it
verdicts.problem: Functions run in Singapore next to Neon only because of a dashboard setting; vercel.json has no regions key and setup section 9 never mentions the region. A re-import or a second project would default to Washington, D.C., where placeOrder's many statements in one transaction risk Prisma's 5-second default timeout.
verdicts.fix: Add "regions": ["sin1"] to vercel.json and one line to setup section 9 step 3. Optionally pass { timeout: 10_000 } to placeOrder's $transaction as a margin.
verdicts.reasoning: Confirmed: vercel.json has only $schema, buildCommand and crons. A live GET on 2026-11-13 to /api/orders/<uuid>/status returned X-Vercel-Id sin1::sin1::..., so the setting is in the dashboard. place.ts:178 calls db.$transaction with no options. Setup step 1 names Singapore for Neon but nothing for Vercel functions. Since the live site is co-located, this is reproducibility hygiene, and low is right.

verdicts.title: Preview deployments are wired to production: same auth URL, site URL and Blob store, and the same database unless Neon branching is on
verdicts.problem: Setup section 9 gives Preview deployments the production BETTER_AUTH_URL, NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL and Blob store, and they share the production database unless the owner turned on Neon preview branching, which nothing records. Vercel builds a preview for every pull request (for example hoshikopi-git-feature-81-demo-mode-xtiannjose.vercel.app on PR #67), so unmerged code can write Guest Orders and Carts into live data, and its links and fake checkout jump to production.
verdicts.fix: Check the Neon integration and either turn on a branch per preview or write in section 9 that previews share production data and are for build checks only. Skip the dynamic baseURL plumbing unless previews are ever used to test sign-in, and connect Blob to Production only if preview uploads should stay out of the live store.
verdicts.reasoning: vercel.json now runs prisma migrate deploy only when VERCEL_ENV is production (7.3), so the destructive half of SEC2-04 and DATA-05 is fixed. auth.ts sets no baseURL; Better Auth 1.7.18 reads BETTER_AUTH_URL (utils/url.mjs:71) and does support baseURL.allowedHosts (create-context.mjs:61). fake.ts:20 and dev/pay actions.ts:26 build URLs from NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL, so an online Order on a preview is sent to production's /dev/pay page and its webhook to production. The vercel[bot] comment on PR #67 shows previews are built and DEPLOYED per PR. Realistic impact is small: Google keys are Production only and emails are dropped, so nobody can sign in on a preview, which rules out Staff, Stars and photo writes; only Guest Orders and Carts could reach production data. Vercel's default Standard Deployment Protection, if still on, limits previews to the owner. Neon branching and protection state need the dashboards.
verdicts.corrections: ADR 0004 and section 9 do not really contradict: roadmap 7.3 and section 9 line 130 record preview branches as the owner's pending switch in the Neon integration, so the fix is to record the outcome, not rewrite the ADR. Photo uploads and Staff writes from a preview are not realistic because sign-in there does not work (links point to production, Google is Production only). The Blob step's 'Development' scope is harmless (local runs have no OIDC token).

verdicts.title: Better Auth's built-in rate limiter counts in memory, so on serverless each function instance has its own counters
verdicts.problem: Better Auth's own per-IP rate limiter keeps its counters in memory, so on Vercel each function instance counts separately and a cold start resets the counts. The routes it guards are already safe for other reasons, so this protects little either way.
verdicts.fix: Keep memory storage and, at most, add one comment in auth.ts saying Better Auth's limits are best effort per instance and the real limits live in src/lib/rate-limit.ts. Do not switch to storage: "database", which collides with the app's own RateLimit model and adds a database write to every auth request.
verdicts.reasoning: Facts confirmed: storage defaults to 'memory' when no secondaryStorage is set (create-context.mjs:175), and auth.ts sets neither. But sending links and starting Google sign-in are disabled HTTP paths (auth.ts:23) that run through Server Actions with the Postgres limiter; auth.api calls from Server Actions do not pass Better Auth's HTTP limiter; the remaining magic-link verify route checks a single-use 32-character token that expires in 5 minutes; the Google callback is state-protected. Fluid compute reuses instances, so counters are not reset per request. Nothing to gain for this demo.
verdicts.corrections: The proposed database storage would not work as written: Better Auth's database limiter uses model "rateLimit" (rate-limiter/index.mjs:80) with key, count and lastRequest fields, which maps to the app's existing Prisma RateLimit model (key, windowStart, count; table rate_limits), so it would need a modelName override and a second table. The auth.ts comment only claims a per-IP limit, which still holds per instance.

verdicts.title: The pg pool has serverless defaults: no connection timeout, and no idle-pool handling for Vercel Fluid compute
verdicts.problem: db.ts hands PrismaPg only a connection string, so pg's pool runs with no connection timeout and a 10 s idle timeout. When all 10 clients are busy, a request waits in the pool's queue with no limit, and a stale socket after a suspended Fluid instance resumes can fail the first query.
verdicts.fix: Pass connectionTimeoutMillis: 5_000 (and optionally idleTimeoutMillis: 5_000) to new PrismaPg({ connectionString, ... }) in db.ts. Add @vercel/functions' attachDatabasePool only if 'Connection terminated unexpectedly' ever shows up in the logs.
verdicts.reasoning: Confirmed: adapter-pg builds new pg2.Pool(this.config) from the string alone (index.mjs:776); pg-pool sets idleTimeoutMillis 10000 (index.js:98) and, without connectionTimeoutMillis, pushes requests to an unbounded pending queue when the pool is full (index.js:206). Counter-evidence: the adapter attaches an 'error' listener to the pool (index.mjs:778-781), so a dropped idle socket is discarded and does not crash the instance; Neon answers a suspended or over-quota compute with a quick error rather than a hang; no connection errors were seen live. Prisma 6's built-in 5 s connect timeout is not carried over by driver adapters, so setting it restores old behaviour. One line, worth doing, impact unproven.
verdicts.corrections: pg-pool index.js:206 is the queue used when the pool is full, not the connect itself; an unreachable host is bounded by OS TCP timeouts and Neon fails fast, so 'wait until the 300 s function limit' is the pool-exhaustion worst case, not the normal outage path. max: 5 is unnecessary behind Neon's pooler. Whether Fluid compute is on needs the Vercel dashboard.

verdicts.title: Open status pages and the Bar Screen poll forever, which keeps Neon Free from scaling to zero and can use up its 100 CU-hours
verdicts.problem: The Order status page queries the database every 5 s while visible, 15 s while hidden and 30 s once Ready, and a Pay at Pickup or Ready Order that nobody closes never stops it. One forgotten desktop tab can keep the Neon Free compute awake around the clock (about 180 CU-hours a month at 0.25 CU against a 100 CU-hour allowance), and Neon then suspends the database, taking every dynamic part of the demo down until the next month.
verdicts.fix: Cap the status poller: stop its interval about 3 hours after the page opened (the visibilitychange handler can still check once when the tab returns), and skip hidden ticks once the Order is Ready since its notification has already fired. Check CU-hour use in the Neon console and note the allowance in setup section 9.
verdicts.reasoning: Each poll runs orderVersion against the database (route.ts). expireUnpaid skips pay_at_pickup Orders (bar.ts:20), so ORD-13 leaves them placed forever, and Ready Orders also stay open until someone hands them over. Chrome throttles hidden timers to about once a minute after 5 minutes, which is still well inside Neon's 5-minute suspend window; mobile browsers freeze background tabs, and laptops sleep. The trigger is unlikely (a desktop tab left open on an awake machine for over two weeks) but the result would take the portfolio link down for weeks. The Neon plan figures come from the auditor's fetch of neon.com/docs/introduction/plans and were not re-fetched; actual use needs the Neon dashboard.
verdicts.corrections: The Bar Screen does not poll in the background: every tick is skipped while document.hidden (bar-screen.tsx:167-169), and it stops once signed out (7.4), so only a visible, signed-in board keeps polling. Simply skipping hidden ticks on the status page would break its 'We'll let you know here when it's ready' notification, which relies on hidden polling, so the cap must be time-based.

verdicts.title: Menu photos go to a public Blob store as uploaded (EXIF kept) and before validation, and replaced or refused uploads are never deleted
verdicts.problem: saveMenuItemAction uploads a menu photo to the public Blob store before the form is validated, as raw bytes that keep any EXIF location, and nothing ever deletes the file a refused save or a replacement leaves behind. The original stays reachable through the url= parameter in next/image's srcset.
verdicts.fix: Validate the form before storing the photo (or store it only after saveMenuItem succeeds), and del the old Blob URL when a save replaces it. Strip metadata by re-encoding with sharp (sharp(bytes).rotate().toBuffer()), which is already installed alongside next, or tell Managers in the upload hint to export photos without location.
verdicts.reasoning: Verified: put('menu/...', Buffer.from(bytes), { access: 'public' }) at photo.ts:63 with no re-encoding; the action calls storeMenuPhoto at actions.ts:71 before saveMenuItem at :75; @vercel/blob is imported only for put in src, with no del anywhere; edit.ts:259 simply overwrites photoUrl. The path traversal half of SEC1-02 and SEC2-08 is fixed (photo.ts:53-58 keeps only a-z0-9- of the slug). Only a Manager past the Second Factor can upload, real photos are on hold (ADR 0012) and the first live upload is still pending (roadmap 5.4), so the exposure is future and small: a photo taken at the invented cafe leaks nothing, one taken at home would.
verdicts.corrections: Re-encoding needs no new library in practice: sharp 0.35.5 is already in node_modules as an optional dependency of next (it would have to be listed in package.json to import it directly).

verdicts.title: No Node version is pinned: no engines field and no .nvmrc, and the docs give three different versions
verdicts.problem: package.json has no engines.node and the repo has no .nvmrc, so the Node major on Vercel comes from a dashboard setting that cannot be seen from the repo. The machine-facts line in docs/08-TOOLING.md says Node 24.19.0 while this computer runs v24.18.0.
verdicts.fix: Add "engines": { "node": "24.x" } to package.json so Vercel uses the same major as development. Update the machine-facts line in docs/08-TOOLING.md to the installed version.
verdicts.reasoning: Verified: no engines or packageManager field, no .nvmrc, .node-version or .tool-versions; node -v gives v24.18.0; Prisma requires ^20.19 || ^22.12 || >=24.0 and Next >=20.9.0. Vercel takes engines.node over the project setting. But every major Vercel offers (20, 22, 24) satisfies Next 16 and Prisma 7, and changing it is a deliberate dashboard action, so real drift is unlikely. A one-line hygiene fix.
verdicts.corrections: The docs do not give three conflicting versions: setup section 1 states a minimum ('22.12 or newer (this computer has 24)'), which is consistent; only the tooling machine-facts line (24.19.0, at docs/08-TOOLING.md:63) is stale against v24.18.0. Downgraded to info because every Node major Vercel offers runs this app.

verdicts.title: Setup section 9 is not the path the live deploy took, and it leaves out region, Node, logs, backups, previews and the cron window
verdicts.problem: Setup section 9 steps 1 and 3 describe copying Neon URLs and setting DATABASE_URL and DIRECT_URL by hand, while the live project gets DATABASE_URL and DATABASE_URL_UNPOOLED from the Vercel Neon integration. The checklist also omits the function region (sin1 live, iad1 is Vercel's default), the Node version, Hobby's 1-hour log retention, backups and restore, and the preview database decision, and section 5 still lacks ALLOW_REMOTE_SEED, DATABASE_URL_UNPOOLED and E2E_DATABASE_URL.
verdicts.fix: Rewrite steps 1 and 3 around the Neon integration with the manual path as an aside, and add one line each for the region (sin1), Node, log retention, backups and the preview database decision. Add the three missing variables to the section 5 table.
verdicts.reasoning: Verified the section 9 text; only step 4's aside and line 130 mention the integration and DATABASE_URL_UNPOOLED; prisma.config.ts:18 falls back to DATABASE_URL_UNPOOLED, seed.ts:15 reads ALLOW_REMOTE_SEED and playwright.config.ts:8 reads E2E_DATABASE_URL, and none is in the section 5 table. Live X-Vercel-Id headers show sin1::sin1, a dashboard setting written nowhere in the repo. For a portfolio project a reproducible deploy doc is part of what is shown, and the edit is small.
verdicts.corrections: The Hobby cron's hour-wide window does not matter here: 22:00 to 22:59 UTC is 6:00 to 6:59 AM Manila, before the seeded 7:00 opening, and unpaid Orders also expire on read (ADR 0007). Step 8's Lighthouse results are recorded in roadmap 5.4, though not in section 9. The substance of region, backups and logs is carried by ops:10, ops:2 and ops:1; this finding is only the doc edit.

verdicts.title: The 'outputFileTracingRoot' / 'turbopack.root' warning comes from a stray lockfile in the user's home folder, not from the project
verdicts.problem: Every local build and start prints a warning about a package-lock.json in C:\Users\cjose, an 84-byte lockfile with an empty packages list that sits outside the repo. Next already ignores it, so it is noise only and does not touch Vercel builds.
verdicts.fix: Delete the empty C:\Users\cjose\package-lock.json; there is no node_modules beside it. Do not add turbopack.root or outputFileTracingRoot to next.config.ts for a machine-only quirk.
verdicts.reasoning: gates/build.log and server-3300.log both show 'Next.js ignored package-lock.json in C:\Users\cjose because it is outside the current Git repository'. The file is 84 bytes, lockfileVersion 3 with packages {}, dated Feb 18 2026, and C:\Users\cjose\node_modules does not exist. Owner's machine housekeeping, not a repo change.

verdicts.title: The 'Becoming real' list omits the hosting move: Vercel Hobby is non-commercial, so a real cafe needs Pro (crons, logs, drains)
verdicts.problem: The PRD's 'Becoming real' row lists a business, BIR receipts, Internet Transactions Act duties, live PayMongo keys and real photos, but not that Vercel Hobby is for non-commercial use only and Neon Free caps compute and restore history. A real cafe would need paid hosting and database plans, which the design already works around (once-a-day cron, expiry on read).
verdicts.fix: Add to that row: Vercel Pro (commercial use, finer crons, longer logs), a paid Neon plan (no compute cap, longer restore window) and error monitoring. One line of docs, no code.
verdicts.reasoning: Verified PRD:203 and roadmap:37 ('Vercel Hobby'). docs/03-ARCHITECTURE.md:153 and ADR 0007 already name Hobby's once-a-day cron as a design driver, so naming the upgrade completes the row's 'listed so nothing in the build blocks it' promise. Hobby's non-commercial fair-use term is long-standing; the other plan details come from the auditor's fetch and were not re-checked. Cheap and strengthens the portfolio story.
verdicts.corrections: A verified Resend domain is already covered by the PRD's 'Email sender' row a few lines up; only the hosting, database and monitoring upgrades are missing.

verdicts.title: Live headers differ from local: Vercel adds Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * to prerendered pages and drops X-Powered-By, and COOP is still missing
verdicts.problem: The live site sends no Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy, and local next start still sends X-Powered-By: Next.js because poweredByHeader is not turned off. Vercel strips X-Powered-By and adds Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * to some prerendered responses, so the earlier audit's header notes hold only for the local server.
verdicts.fix: Add { key: "Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy", value: "same-origin" } to the headers list and poweredByHeader: false to next.config.ts. Leave the CDN's ACAO alone: it allows no credentialed reads, and those pages are public anyway.
verdicts.reasoning: Live GETs on 2026-11-13: /menu (X-Nextjs-Prerender: 1, STALE) and a prerendered 404 carried ACAO *; / (HIT) and /events/latte-art-night/calendar (MISS) did not; no response had X-Powered-By or COOP; CSP, HSTS, X-Frame-Options and Permissions-Policy are present; X-Vercel-Id shows sin1. Local :3300 /menu sends X-Powered-By: Next.js and Cache-Control: private, no-cache, no-store. COOP same-origin does not affect the PayMongo redirect or Google sign-in, which are full navigations.
verdicts.corrections: ACAO * is not on every prerendered response: / served from the cache (HIT) had none today, while /menu (STALE) and the prerendered 404 did. It is Vercel CDN behaviour, not app configuration.

verdicts.title: A Manager without a fresh Second Factor sees Pause, Busy and Cancel on the Bar Screen; a tap drops the action, leaves the board and ends on /manage/hours
verdicts.problem: On the Bar Screen, a Manager whose session has not passed the Second Factor still sees Pause, Busy Mode and Cancel, because the page shows these controls by role alone. A tap goes to /manage/two-factor and drops the action, and after the code the Manager lands on /manage/hours or /manage/orders with nothing applied.
verdicts.fix: Pass into BarScreen whether the session has passed the Second Factor, and show the Manager controls only then, with a short link to enter the code otherwise. Add an e2e test for a Manager without the Second Factor on /bar.
verdicts.reasoning: bar/page.tsx calls requireStaff('barista', '/bar'), which skips the Second Factor, then passes manager={staff.role === 'manager'}. pauseAction, resumeAction, busyAction and endBusyAction call requireStaff('manager', '/manage/hours'), and cancelAtBar calls requireStaff('manager', '/manage/orders'). Both redirect to /manage/two-factor when secondFactorPassed is false. staffAwaitingSecondFactor accepts only /manage targets, so the flow can never return to /bar or replay the tap. The only Busy Mode e2e test (bar.spec.ts:114) signs in through /manage first, so this path is untested. Roadmap 8.10 lists 'the Bar Screen Second Factor redirect, a bug listed for its own fix' under Dropped, so the bug is known but no finding records it. The redirect fails closed, so access control is not at risk. The bug is a lost action at a busy moment, and it pushes the Manager to enter a code on the shared tablet (ID2-02). The auditor's run.log shows both redirects (/manage/two-factor?next=%2Fmanage%2Fhours and %2Fmanage%2Forders).
verdicts.corrections: None of substance. ID2-02 and ID1-04 already mention the Bar cancel needing the code on the tablet; this finding adds the lost action and the wrong landing page. Hiding the controls without the Second Factor also removes the reason to enter Manager codes on the tablet.

verdicts.title: Public menu takes about a minute or two to show a Sold Out or a Hidden item, not 'within seconds'
verdicts.problem: A Staff save sometimes takes one to two minutes to reach the public menu: the audit timed 60 s for a Sold Out and 117 s for a Hide. docs/03 promises 'within seconds' and PRD MENU-04 'within a minute'; checkout re-prices on the server and refuses Sold Out or Hidden items, so the cost is a late refusal, not a wrong Order.
verdicts.fix: Give the menu readers a custom cacheLife profile with a short revalidate (for example 10 s, with expire kept at 5 minutes or more so pages stay prerendered), stop menuSlugs wrapping getMenu, and make the e2e check fail after about 15 s. Then correct docs/03 line 77 to the bound the code actually keeps.
verdicts.reasoning: Every menu Server Action calls updateTag('menu') after its write. All four menu readers (getMenu, getMenuItem, menuSlugs, getPricedOptions) use 'use cache' with cacheTag('menu') and cacheLife('minutes'): stale 5 min, revalidate 1 min, expire 1 h (node_modules/next/dist/docs cacheLife.md). The cron adds revalidateTag('menu', 'max'). docs/03:77 admits that a save racing a cache refill can store old data as fresh and 'heals within a minute'. The e2e helper's comment says a save under another tag at the same moment can delay it until the lifetime runs out, and the helper waits 150 s. A stale entry healing at the 60 s revalidate matches the 60.6 s Sold Out. The 117 s Hide most likely comes from two stale-while-revalidate layers stacked: the route regenerates at 60 s from a getMenu entry that is itself stale, and menuSlugs nests getMenu. That case breaks the PRD's one-minute bound. I could not rerun it, since the rules forbid saving through the Staff tools. The tests reviewer's serial e2e run saw 12 to 14 s, so the normal path is fast and the slow cases are the race. Other reviewers were saving under other tags during the audit (for example Event Sign-ups call updateTag('content')), which is the trigger the e2e comment names. The auditor's 'these were not two saves a moment apart' therefore does not rule out the documented race.
verdicts.corrections: Measure against PRD MENU-04 ('prices and Sold Out update within a minute of a change'), not only docs/03's 'within seconds'. Only the 117 s Hide breaks the PRD; the 60.6 s Sold Out is the documented one-minute heal. Severity is lowered to low because priceChoices refuses Sold Out and Hidden items at add and checkout (menu pricing.ts:94-131). The cause is most likely the known refill race lengthened by nested caches, with concurrent saves by other reviewers as the trigger, not a new failure of updateTag.

verdicts.title: Two different numbers are both called 'Sales' for the same day (Orders and the Today strip vs Reports)
verdicts.problem: /manage/orders and the /manage Today strip total every Order not cancelled, expired or refunded, including unpaid online Orders still Placed and Pay at Pickup not yet collected, and the Orders page labels that 'Sales'. /manage/reports labels only Picked Up Orders 'Sales', so one day shows two different 'Sales' figures.
verdicts.fix: Add 'Sales' to GLOSSARY.md as the total of Picked Up Orders and keep that meaning on Reports. Rename the Orders tile and Today strip figure to something like 'Booked today', with a note that Pay at Pickup still to collect is inside it.
verdicts.reasoning: dayOrders filters service_day = the day and status not in cancelled, expired or refunded. It therefore sums placed (including online Orders awaiting payment), paid, accepted, preparing, ready and picked_up; the Today strip reuses it. salesReport sums status = 'picked_up' only, grouped by the placed_at Manila day. Neither GLOSSARY.md nor the PRD defines 'Sales'. STAFF-07 asks for 'a day's Orders and totals', which matches dayOrders. STAFF-08 asks for 'sales by day', which matches Reports, and Reports' meaning (completed takings) is the conventional one. Grouping by service_day or by placed_at gives the same day today, because Orders can only be placed for the same day until ordering for tomorrow exists.
verdicts.corrections: Severity is lowered to low because each figure states its rule on screen. The Orders tile notes 'Cancelled, expired and refunded Orders are left out', and Reports says 'Picked Up Orders by the day they were placed'. So the problem is one word used for two things, not a wrong number. The service_day versus placed_at difference is moot today.

verdicts.title: Busy Mode is invisible and cannot be ended outside the Bar Screen, and the Prep Time example ignores it
verdicts.problem: Busy Mode shows only on the Bar Screen and to customers. /manage/hours, the /manage Today strip and the Prep Time example all ignore it, and Start and End Busy Mode exist only on /bar, so a Manager on /manage cannot see that customer times are longer.
verdicts.fix: Add busyMinutes and busyUntil to getHoursForStaff, or reuse getOrderingDay's busy, and show them in the Today strip's Ordering tile and on /manage/hours with an End Busy Mode button. Reword the example to 'Example: with 4 drinks ahead' and include the Busy minutes while Busy Mode runs.
verdicts.reasoning: getHoursForStaff returns prep without busyMinutes, so prepMinutes(4, hours.prep) adds 0. The label 'Right now: with 4 drinks ahead' describes a fixed example, not the live queue. The /manage Ordering tile uses orderingState, which does not know about Busy Mode. busyAction and endBusyAction are imported only by bar-screen.tsx. Roadmap 8.4 placed Busy Mode on the Bar Screen next to Pause on purpose. Pause also appears on /manage/hours, though, so its absence there is an inconsistency.
verdicts.corrections: Severity is lowered to low. Busy Mode ends by itself after 30 or 60 minutes, and /bar opens on any device with a Manager session, so a Manager away from the bar can still end it there. Putting the controls on the Bar Screen was the 8.4 design; the gap is only that /manage does not show it.

verdicts.title: Blank or decimal Hours and Capacity inputs save silently: a cleared Capacity cell becomes 0 drinks, a blank map pin becomes 0,0, Prep Time is rounded
verdicts.problem: On /manage/hours and /manage/cafe, the server turns a blank required number into 0. A cleared Capacity cell saves 0 drinks for that weekday, so no customer gets a Pickup Time, and a blank map pin saves 0,0; both show 'Saved'.
verdicts.fix: Treat an empty string as missing before coercion, for example with z.preprocess that maps '' to undefined, for Capacity, Prep Time and the map pin, and add required to those inputs. Refuse Prep Time with more than one decimal place, and Special Hours dates before today.
verdicts.reasoning: count and minutes in save-hours.ts and mapLat and mapLng in save-details.ts are z.coerce.number(). I checked with the project's zod that '' parses as { success: true, data: 0 } for both. The Capacity cells have only min and max, and the map pin inputs are type text with no required. Capacity 0 passes the database CHECK (>= 0). pickupWindows then finds no room for any drink, so checkout offers no Pickup Times all day. prep_*_minutes is Decimal(4,1), so 1.25 is stored as 1.3. SpecialInput uses z.iso.date with no lower bound; only the date input has min={today}.
verdicts.corrections: The Prep Time rounding and past Special Hours dates are cosmetic. Past Special Hours rows are never read, since getHoursForStaff lists only today onwards. The cleared Capacity cell and the blank map pin carry the impact.

verdicts.title: No upper bound on prices: a Base Price, Price Delta or Event price above PHP 21,474,836 crashes the editor and the typed form is lost; a typo like 1650 for 165 saves silently
verdicts.problem: A Base Price, Price Delta or Event price above PHP 21,474,836.47 passes validation but overflows the Int column. The save fails with a 500, the global error page replaces the form, and everything typed is lost.
verdicts.fix: Add an upper bound to the shared pesos() schema in menu edit.ts and to the Event price check in content.ts, for example PHP 100,000, with a friendly message. A warning for large price jumps is optional polish, not a fix.
verdicts.reasoning: parsePesos returns any safe integer. pesos() in edit.ts and the Event refine in content.ts only check that it is not null. base_cents, delta_cents and price_cents are Int, with a maximum of 2,147,483,647 centavos. The auditor's run.log shows the HTTP 500 and React error #441 for the Event price, and the menu cases follow the same code path. A Promo price must be below the Base Price (edit.ts:185), so it cannot overflow on its own.
verdicts.corrections: Severity is lowered to low: it takes an eight-digit peso amount in a Manager-only form, and nothing is saved. The '1650 for 165' cap is a product idea, not a defect; a fixed plausibility cap would refuse real prices such as merchandise or event packages.

verdicts.title: A refused cancel on /manage/orders says the Order 'can't be refunded now'
verdicts.problem: When a Manager's cancel on /manage/orders is refused, because the reason is blank once trimmed or the Order has already changed, the page says the Order 'can't be refunded now'. The message is about a refund nobody asked for and hides the real reason.
verdicts.fix: Give cancelAction its own outcomes, such as cancel_reason ('Write a reason the Customer will see') and cancel_not_allowed ('K-019 was already cancelled or picked up'). Map them in the page's message switch.
verdicts.reasoning: cancelAction sends every cancelOrder failure to done=not_allowed. The page renders refund copy for not_allowed, which it shares with refundAction. The reason input is required, but a value of only spaces passes that check, and the server then refuses it as reason_required.

verdicts.title: A Barista can only mark Sold Out behind the Second Factor; the Bar Screen's 'Sold out?' link opens Annika's pending authenticator secret on the shared tablet
verdicts.problem: Baristas can mark Sold Out only at /manage/menu, behind the Second Factor, so STAFF-03 works only after the Barista enrols an authenticator; the seeded Barista never has. On the always-signed-in bar tablet, the Bar Screen's 'Sold out?' link opens that Barista's pending QR code and setup key.
verdicts.fix: Add Sold Out and Back on to the Bar Screen through a /bar Server Action that calls setMenuItemSoldOut and setOptionSoldOut under requireStaff('barista', '/bar'), and record this as an update to ADR 0005 and docs/03. Until then, hide the 'Sold out?' link from a Barista who has not enrolled.
verdicts.reasoning: toggleSoldOut uses requireStaff('barista', '/manage/menu'), which demands the Second Factor. In the database, annika@'s two_factors row is unconfirmed since 2026-11-05. The Bar header links 'Sold out?' to /manage/menu, and the two-factor page shows the pending secret's QR code and setup key. On product fit, STAFF-03 is MVP. The Glossary says a Barista marks Menu Items Sold Out. Research C-03 says Sold Out is 'toggled from the Bar Screen' (MVP), and C-12 lists 'Sold Out toggles' on the Bar Screen. ADR 0005 lets Baristas use /bar without TOTP, so a bar-only Sold Out action does not contradict it. docs/03:67 now records the current placement ('Baristas open /manage (Today) and /manage/menu for Sold Out'), so the move needs that line and an ADR note changed. It is a worthwhile change for the Barista persona at little cost.
verdicts.corrections: Severity is lowered to low. The secret-exposure risk is overstated: anyone who can tap the tablet already holds the Barista's signed-in session, and enrolling unlocks only Today and Sold Out. First-come enrolment is already ID1-13, and the design gap is DOC-16, which docs/03 later answered by recording the current choice.

verdicts.title: Nothing in the Staff tools can be deleted or archived: Menu Items, Categories, Option Groups, Options, Events, Posts, Recurring Events and Inquiries
verdicts.problem: No Staff record can be deleted, and Options and Option Groups cannot be hidden either. A mistyped or discontinued Option therefore stays on every Menu Item that uses its group, and test records stay in every Staff list.
verdicts.fix: Add an is_hidden flag to options, left out of the menu and refused by priceChoices. Add an audited Delete for records nothing references, such as never-ordered Menu Items, unused Option Groups and draft Posts.
verdicts.reasoning: A grep finds only deleteSpecialHoursAction as a delete. Most types can already be archived, though: Category.isHidden and MenuItem.isHidden, Event.isPublished, RecurringEvent.isPublished, Post.publishedAt (null means draft), and Inquiry status with Close. Option has no such flag, and an Option Group can only be unticked from each Menu Item. PRD STAFF-04 and STAFF-06 ask Managers to edit and write, not to delete. Order Lines snapshot names and prices, and order_lines.menu_item_id is SetNull, so deletes would not change history.
verdicts.corrections: The title overstates the gap. Menu Items and Categories can be Hidden, Events, Recurring Events and Posts can be unpublished, and Inquiries can be closed, so only Options and Option Groups lack an archive. Severity is lowered to low; the real gaps are Options and the clutter of never being able to delete.

verdicts.title: Event Sign-ups are read-only for the Manager: no remove, no add for a walk-in or phone call, no 'email everyone', and unpublishing an Event tells nobody
verdicts.problem: The Manager's Sign-ups panel is read only, so a Manager cannot remove a Sign-up or copy all the guests' emails. Unpublishing an Event, or lowering its seats below those taken, gives no warning and tells nobody.
verdicts.fix: Add an audited Remove button per Sign-up, using the same delete as cancelSignup, and a 'Copy all emails' or mailto link for the confirmed guests. Warn on save when the seats fall below those taken, or when an Event with Sign-ups is unpublished.
verdicts.reasoning: The panel's comment says 'Read only: guests confirm and cancel by their link', so this was a deliberate 8.7 choice. cancelSignup needs the guest's token. saveEvent does not check the new seats against Sign-ups or warn on unpublishing. EVT-02 (V1, S) asks only for a cap and a confirmation email, so these tools go beyond the PRD. Since 8.7, unconfirmed Sign-ups hold seats for only 30 minutes and guests can cancel by link, which reduces the spam (SEC2-02) and phone-cancel cases. Remove and Copy emails are cheap and worth adding. Adding a Sign-up by hand and a Cancel Event mail-out add little for a concept cafe with no real guests.
verdicts.corrections: Severity is lowered to low, and effort to S for the parts worth building. The 8.7 email confirmation and cancel link already cover much of the impact cited from SEC2-02 and FEAT-05. 'Email everyone' and a 'Cancel Event' mail-out are out of scope for the portfolio demo.

verdicts.title: The 'Up to 50 at a time' Stars cap is only a browser attribute; a Manager can still give any amount, including to themselves
verdicts.problem: The Stars form says 'Up to 50 at a time' and sets min and max on the input, but adjustStars checks only for a non-zero integer, so any amount saves. memberByEmail also finds Staff, so a Manager can give Stars to their own account.
verdicts.fix: Enforce a limit of 50 Stars either way in adjustStars, refuse a memberId equal to the actor's id, and show both refusals from the server. Add one database test for each.
verdicts.reasoning: adjustStars checks the role, the reason, and Number.isInteger(stars) && stars !== 0, with no upper bound and no self check. The form's min and max are only browser attributes. memberByEmail matches any user that is not deleted, Staff included. This is the open issue ID1-14 / ID2-11, plus a UI hint that promises a limit the server does not enforce. It stays low because the action is Manager-only, behind the Second Factor, and audited with a reason.

verdicts.title: Reports: the 30-day view is a 30-row table with bars squeezed under the day labels, Star adjustments are netted to zero, and the 'Cancelled' and 'Refunded' links open today's Orders
verdicts.problem: On /manage/reports, Star adjustments show only their net sum, so +51 and -51 read as 0 and hide the Stars a Manager handed out. The Cancelled and Refunded counts cover the whole range but link to today's Orders.
verdicts.fix: Show adjustments as '+N given, -M taken' from two sums in the loyalty report. Drop the links on the range counts, or link them to a filtered Orders view.
verdicts.reasoning: In the loyalty report, adjusted is sum('adjust'), a net figure. The Cancelled and Refunded labels link to /manage/orders, which opens today. STAFF-08 asks for 'sales by day, top Menu Items, Stars issued and redeemed', and the page covers all of them. Netting the adjustments hides the Stars issued by hand, the figure an owner would check. The Bar under each day label is a deliberate sparkline-style design. Sales by hour, a Pay at Pickup versus online split and a CSV export go beyond STAFF-08. Fraunces for the figures is a taste point: docs/05 asks for tabular sans only for prices in tables.
verdicts.corrections: Only the netted adjustments and the range counts that link to today are defects. The 30-row table, the typography, the hour-of-day chart and the CSV export are taste or added scope. The effort is S for the two fixes.

verdicts.title: Order Codes break across lines on a landscape tablet ('K-' / '018'), and portrait tablets push Making and Ready below the fold
verdicts.problem: On a 1024 px landscape tablet the Bar card squeezes the Order Code and the 'ASAP, placed 2:46 PM' block into one flex row, so the code breaks at its hyphen into 'K-' and '018'. Below 1024 px the three lanes stack, so on a portrait tablet a few New Orders push Ready (the Orders to hand over) below the fold.
verdicts.fix: Give the Order Code `whitespace-nowrap shrink-0` and let the time block wrap under it (`flex-wrap`). Optionally use a New | Making and Ready two-column layout from md (768 px) so Ready stays on screen in portrait.
verdicts.reasoning:
Card header is `flex items-baseline justify-between gap-3` with `

{order.code}

` and a right-aligned span; both flex items can shrink to min-content, and the hyphen in 'K-018' is a line-break opportunity. The saved screenshot bar-annika-1024x768-ready.png shows 'K-' / '018' and 'placed 2:46 / PM'. The lane grid is `grid gap-4 lg:grid-cols-3`, so at 768 px the lanes stack; bar-annika-768-three.png shows Making at about y=659 and Ready at about y=767 of 1024 with two New Orders. docs/05 section 9 says 'landscape first' and the wireframe used a 1194 px tablet, but 1024x768 is the common iPad landscape size, so the wrap is in the primary orientation.

verdicts.title: Bar cards show when an ASAP Order was placed but not when it is due, never flag late Orders, and list every default Option
verdicts.problem: An ASAP card shows only when the Order was placed, never the Pickup Time the Customer was promised, and no card changes when that time has passed. Baristas cannot see which Orders are running late.
verdicts.fix: On ASAP cards show 'due 3:00 PM' from windowStart, which barBoard already sends, and tint the card once that time has passed (a re-render on the existing 30 s clock tick). Leave the per-Order 'Running late' tap to its own batch, as roadmap 8.4 already notes.
verdicts.reasoning: The due/late part holds: BarOrder carries windowStart, and the card renders `ASAP, placed {placedAt}` only; nothing compares the time with now. For an ASAP Order windowStart is the first offered Pickup Window (place.ts:235), the time on the Customer's page. Roadmap 8.4 lists the per-Order 'Running late' tap as not done, not rejected. The default-Options part does not hold up as an S change: the Order Line snapshot stores only {group, name, deltaCents} (place.ts:95-99), with no isDefault, and reading the live menu would break the 'Orders snapshot names, Options and prices' rule. docs/05 section 9 specifies Lines with Options as short tags ('L · Oat · 50% · Less ice'), and the size is needed even when it is the default.
verdicts.corrections: Drop or defer 'send only non-default Options': it needs isDefault added to the Order Line snapshot (effort M) and contradicts the docs/05 section 9 card spec; at most, bold the non-default ones once the snapshot records it. Note journeys:10: the ASAP window can be later than the 'about 5 min' quote, so the due time shown should be the same window the Customer's page shows.

verdicts.title: Markdown lists and headings render unstyled in the preview and on public Event, Post and Visit pages
verdicts.problem: Markdown lists and headings show as plain lines with no bullets, numbers or heading sizes, both in the editor preview and on the public Event, Post and Visit pages, even though the editor hint promises '- lists'. A '#' heading also adds a second h1 to the public page.
verdicts.fix: Style ul, ol, li and h2 to h4 inside the shared Markdown component (for example `[&_ul]:list-disc [&_ol]:list-decimal [&_ul,&_ol]:pl-6` plus heading sizes) and map h1 to h2 through react-markdown's `components`. Render the preview with that same Markdown component so preview and page match.
verdicts.reasoning: markdown.tsx wraps `<ReactMarkdown skipHtml>` in a div that styles only links (`[&_a]:underline`), and markdown-field.tsx renders its own ReactMarkdown with the same link-only style. Tailwind 4 preflight sets `list-style: none` on ul and ol and makes headings inherit size and weight, and globals.css has no list or heading rules for Markdown. The saved post-preview.png shows 'Big heading' and 'one / two' as plain text. The component is used on /cafe (three fields), /events/[slug] and /news/[slug]. The seeded content has no lists, which is why nobody noticed.

verdicts.title: Staff page: no Second Factor status or reset, and only the 'Member' choice warns that the person is signed out
verdicts.problem: The Add Staff form defaults to Barista and does not say when the email already belongs to a Manager, so 'Give role' can quietly demote a colleague and sign them out. On a row, only the Member choice warns about the sign-out, although any lower role ends the person's sessions.
verdicts.fix: Show the warning for any choice that ranks below the person's current role, and in Add Staff answer 'already a Manager' (or ask to confirm) before lowering an existing role. Optionally show 'Authenticator set up / waiting' per person; a Manager-led reset needs an ADR 0014 amendment first.
verdicts.reasoning: setRole ends sessions whenever `RANK[role] < RANK[person.role]` (staff.ts:59-61); role-form.tsx shows 'They lose staff access and are signed out now.' only when `chosen === "customer"`; the Add Staff select defaults to `role ?? "barista"` and setRole accepts an existing Manager's email. The page intro says 'Taking a role away signs them out at once', so the rule is stated in general, but not at the moment of choosing. The database shows Annika's two_factors row pending (confirmed_at null) since 2026-11-05, and nothing on /manage/staff shows it.
verdicts.corrections: The Second Factor reset is a recorded decision, not a missing feature: ADR 0014's Consequences send a lost phone to SQL run by whoever runs the database (docs/06-SETUP.md section 6), and batch 8.5 deliberately covered roles and sign-out only. Recommending it means amending ADR 0014 (audited delete of the two_factors row plus ending sessions, with tests), so effort M for that part and optional for a portfolio demo. The demotion warning is the part worth doing.

verdicts.title: 'Sign out everywhere' copy promises 'at once', but the Bar Screen keeps working for up to 5 minutes
verdicts.problem: 'Sign out everywhere' tells the Manager the person is signed out on every device, but the Bar Screen, /api/bar and the bar's one-tap moves keep working for up to 5 minutes. Better Auth trusts the signed session cookie cache until it expires and never re-reads the deleted session row on those routes.
verdicts.fix: Pass `query: { disableCookieCache: true }` to getSession in the Staff guards (requireStaff and currentStaff), which costs one indexed session read per request. If that cost is unwanted, change the copy to 'signed out within 5 minutes'.
verdicts.reasoning: auth.ts sets `cookieCache: { enabled: true, maxAge: 5 * 60 }`. In better-auth 1.7.18, getSession returns the cached session from the session_data cookie without a database read until it expires (api/routes/session.mjs:55-150), and refreshCache is off by default, so the window is bounded at 5 minutes. endSessions only deletes session rows. currentUser re-reads users.role on every call, so role removal does stop /bar, /api/bar and bar actions at once. /manage pages call secondFactorPassed, which reads the session row and fails for a deleted session, so /manage is also blocked at once. Only the /bar routes, which skip the Second Factor (ADR 0014), keep working. ID1-07 reproduced the same 5-minute gap live after revoke-sessions.
verdicts.corrections: The 'at once' sentence (page.tsx:22, 'Taking a role away signs them out at once') is about role removal, which does take effect at once because the role is re-read from the database. The overpromise is the Sign out everywhere text ('They are signed out on every phone and computer', team-list.tsx:143) and its success line ('is signed out on every device', actions.ts:61). The impact is also narrower than 'keep moving Orders' implies: a lost tablet keeps only Barista-level Bar Screen access, for at most 5 minutes.

verdicts.title: A Pay at Pickup refund records no Refund row and never tells the Manager to hand the cash back
verdicts.problem: Refunding a Pay at Pickup Order asks 'Refund PHP 240 in full?' and then says 'Refunded K-018', with nothing telling the Manager to give the cash back. Meanwhile the Customer's email says 'We refund it at the counter.'
verdicts.fix: For Pay at Pickup Orders, word the confirm as 'Give PHP 240 back in cash, then confirm' and the result as 'Refunded K-018 in cash.' Keep the refunds table for provider refunds, as docs/03 and docs/04 define it.
verdicts.reasoning: refundPayment returns 'no_online_payment' when the Order has no Payment row, and refundOrder then moves the Order to Refunded and emails the Customer. The orders page shows the same confirm and done copy for every Payment Method. orderRefundedEmail says 'We refund it at the counter.' for pay_at_pickup, so the Customer is told to expect cash while the Manager is never prompted to hand it over. docs/03 section 7 defines the refund for Pay at Pickup as 'cash at the counter', with no provider call.
verdicts.corrections: The missing Refund row is by design, not a gap. refunds.payment_id is a required FK to payments, payments holds 'one online Payment per Order' with provider paymongo or fake (docs/04), and docs/03 says the Refund row 'records the provider refund id'. A 'cash' Refund row would need a schema change against the data model. 'Missing from any refund list or reconciliation' is wrong: no screen reads the refunds table. The Orders list, the 'Cancelled or refunded' count and Reports' Refunded count all use Order Status, and order_events records who refunded. Only the Manager-facing copy is the gap.

verdicts.title: Closing a day on Opening Hours still demands its opening, last-order and closing times
verdicts.problem: Saving Opening Hours with a day ticked Closed still requires that day's three times, so a Manager who clears them gets 'Enter opening, last order and closing.' and nothing saves. The form greys those times out when Closed is ticked, which suggests they do not matter.
verdicts.fix: When isClosed is set, accept empty times and keep the stored values, since opening_hours columns are NOT NULL. Special Hours already treats its times as optional when closed.
verdicts.reasoning: WeeklyRow requires `opensAt: time, lastOrderAt: time, closesAt: time` regardless of isClosed, and a failed parse sets the 'Enter opening, last order and closing.' error before the isClosed check. SpecialInput has optional times and a refine that skips them when closed. The form prefills each time from the saved row, so the error appears only when a Manager clears a time on a Closed day, as the auditor did (hours-closed-blank.png). This is a narrow trigger, but a real validation inconsistency.

verdicts.title: The Barista Pick limit counts Hidden and seasonal-ended items and does not say which three hold the slots
verdicts.problem: When the three Day or Night Barista Picks are taken, the menu editor says 'Untick one of them first' without naming them, and the menu list does not show which items carry a pick. A Seasonal item whose date has passed keeps its pick, so Home shows only two picks and the Manager is still told the slots are full.
verdicts.fix: Name the current picks in the error, with links to their editors. Leave items whose Seasonal date has passed out of the count, or clear their pick badge when the season ends.
verdicts.reasoning: The count is `db.menuItem.count({ where: { badges: { has: pick } ... } })`, with no isHidden or availableUntil filter. Home filters getMenu's visible, in-season items by picks.day or picks.night with no cap (page.tsx:36). PICK_FULL names no items, and /manage/menu lists items without their badges. The database currently has exactly three visible Day picks and three visible Night picks, so nothing is wrong today. The auditor's live refusal came from a full set of visible picks, not a hidden one holding a slot.
verdicts.corrections: Counting Hidden items is defensible: a hidden pick returns to Home when un-hidden, and Home has no cap of three, so leaving Hidden items out of the count would let Home show four or more picks after an un-hide (that fix would also need `slice(0, 3)` on Home). The clean defects are the unnamed picks and an ended Seasonal item holding a slot.

verdicts.title: Submitting the sign-in form quickly after the page loads drops ?next=, so Staff land on /account instead of /bar or /manage
verdicts.problem: No defect: the sign-in form always posts the `next` from the URL, even when it is submitted before the page hydrates. The /account landings came from the audit scripts, not the app.
verdicts.fix: Nothing to change in the app. Drop the finding.
verdicts.reasoning: The hidden field is rendered on the server from `safeNext(searchParams.next)` inside the streamed Form, so it carries the right value from the first byte, and React's progressive enhancement posts it even before hydration. I ran 10 submissions with the POST intercepted and aborted, so no email was sent: 7 at commit, domcontentloaded and networkidle, and 3 under 6x CPU and slow-network throttling, filled before hydration. Every one posted the requested /bar or /manage. The original scripts signin.mjs and signin2.mjs default `next = "/account"` when the third argument is left out, and run.log never records the URL they opened. The two failures match that default, while the scripts that passed next (next-probe3 and signin3) posted and landed on /bar, and 50 ms sampling never saw /account.
verdicts.corrections: The cause was most likely the audit scripts' default argument (`const [email, name, next = "/account"] = process.argv.slice(2)`), not a race in the app. Scripts: verify/staff-2/next-race.mjs and next-race-slow.mjs.

verdicts.title: The new-Order chime may stay silent after the tablet reloads until someone taps the screen
verdicts.problem: After the Bar Screen reloads, each chime builds a new AudioContext with no user tap and never calls resume(), and Chrome's and Safari's autoplay rules start such a context suspended. The first new Orders after a reload therefore arrive with no sound until someone touches the board, and the try/catch hides it.
verdicts.fix: Keep one module-level AudioContext, create it on the first tap (the Sound button or any tap on the board), and call resume() before each chime. While its state is 'suspended', show 'Tap to turn on sound'.
verdicts.reasoning: chime() runs `new AudioContext()` on every arrival and never checks state or calls resume(). Chrome's documented autoplay policy creates an AudioContext made before any user activation in the 'suspended' state, and iPadOS Safari needs a gesture; after the first tap (sticky activation), later contexts start running, so the silent window runs from a reload to the first tap. Playwright's Chromium does not enforce the policy: an AudioContext reported 'running' before any tap even with --autoplay-policy=user-gesture-required (verify/staff-2/audio-policy.mjs), so a headless test cannot reproduce it. The verdict rests on the code and the documented browser policy. The Order page's status-poller.tsx already uses the safer pattern of one module-level context created on a tap.
verdicts.corrections: Same root cause and same fix as motion:6 (a new AudioContext per chime); merge the two. A tablet that sleeps (FEAT-11) is a separate cause of missed chimes.

verdicts.title: Access control on the Staff tools holds, including the 8.4 and 8.5 Server Actions

verdicts.fix: Add one table-driven access test that calls each Staff action as a Member, a Barista and a Manager without the Second Factor, with harmless ids, and expects 404 or the redirect. Add db tests that setRole and endSessions by a Barista return not_allowed.

verdicts.title: No test protects the Prep Time queue: a mutant that ignores the drinks on the bar passes every placement, bar and Prep Time test
verdicts.problem: No test puts drinks in Accepted or Preparing Orders before placing an Order or reading the Bar Screen, so the queued-drinks part of Prep Time (drinksQueuedAhead) is never checked. A change that counts the wrong statuses or days, or stops passing the queue to placement, would leave every test green.
verdicts.fix: Add one DB test in place-order.test.ts with the clock at 9:00: 4 drinks Accepted and 4 Preparing give Prep Time 20, so ASAP lands in 9:30 instead of 9:15, and adding Placed, Ready and yesterday's drinks changes nothing. Add one bar.test case where queued drinks make a Scheduled Order make-next earlier.
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced from the saved logs: mutant-queue0.ts mocks windows.ts so the queue is always 0, and mutant-queue0.log shows 'Test Files 9 passed (9), Tests 66 passed (66)'. The control mutant-queue40.log fails 5 tests, so the mock reached placeOrder and barBoard. In the repo, place-order.test.ts:105-111 and bar.test.ts:92-101 run only with an empty queue. ordering-day.test.ts unit-tests prepMinutes(4, ...) but not drinksQueuedAhead. checkoutView (reads.ts) has no DB test at all, and no e2e test asserts a Prep Time value. No test anywhere would fail. Busy Mode is better covered than the finding says: cafe-admin.test.ts:112 checks getOrderingDay returns busyMinutes, and placement reads the same day.prep, so only the queue term is unprotected. The code is correct today, so the risk is a future regression, not a live defect.
verdicts.corrections: Severity high to medium: the code is correct today and the risk is a future regression, not a live defect. Busy Mode in placement is covered indirectly through getOrderingDay (cafe-admin.test.ts:112) plus prepMinutes, so a dedicated Busy Mode placement test is optional. bar.test.ts make-next case is lines 92-101. Related but not the same: DOC-04 (how Prep Time is defined) and PERF-11 (barBoard version test, fixed in 7.4).

verdicts.title: The Star refund floor ('Stars already spent stay spent') has no test: a mutant that takes the balance below zero passes all 42 Star and refund tests
verdicts.problem: reverseForOrder stops a Refund from taking a Member's Star balance below zero (Math.min with the balance), but no test refunds an Order after its Stars were spent. If that floor is dropped, a Member who redeemed their Stars and then had an Order refunded would show a negative balance, and the suite stays green.
verdicts.fix: Add one case to stars.test.ts: earn 2 Stars on Order A, spend them (a Manager adjust of -2 or a Reward), refund A, and expect balance 0 with no reverse row. That pins the floor in about ten lines.
verdicts.reasoning: ledger.ts:74 holds 'const take = Math.min(net, await balance(memberId, tx))'. The only reverse test (stars.test.ts:101-111) refunds Stars that were not spent (2 to 0). mutant-reverse.log, which reverses the full net with no floor, shows 'Test Files 7 passed (7), Tests 42 passed (42)'. The control mutant-noreverse.log fails 'takes the Stars back when a picked-up Order is Refunded', so the mock reached the code. No database CHECK or trigger can stop a negative sum: star_entries has only a sign check. The gap is real. The consequence of a regression is small: the balance shows negative and canRedeem (balance >= 9) still refuses, so no free drinks and no money are involved, and the path (spend, then a Refund after pickup) is rare.
verdicts.corrections: Severity medium to low: a regression would show a negative balance on a rare path, with no money and no extra Rewards. The finding's 'refund again' step cannot happen: refunded is terminal, so drop it. Line range of reverseForOrder is 63-79. DATA-04 (no database backstop for duplicate Star rows) is related, not the same problem.

verdicts.title: transition() matches the docs table today, but tests pin only about 25 of 1,026 state, target and actor cases, and never Demo Mode switched off

The gap is refusals plus the one demoMode guard. The demo tests end at customer-order.test.ts:247.
