verdicts.title: e2e shared state: pause, Busy Mode, a price change and a growing Prep Time queue hit specs that order in other workers; today's green run was file-order luck
verdicts.problem: With fullyParallel and 4 workers, some specs change cafe-wide state while specs in other workers place Orders. These are the pause in manage-hours, Busy Mode in bar.spec, the Spanish Latte price in manage-menu, and Orders left Preparing by SQL in order-status, so a full e2e run fails at random.
verdicts.fix: Move the cafe-wide mutators into one serial spec that runs as its own project after the others (dependencies), and restore pause, Busy Mode and the price in afterEach. Pick Scheduled windows well clear of Prep Time instead of .first(), and set trace to 'retain-on-failure' so the next flake leaves evidence.
verdicts.reasoning: playwright.config.ts has fullyParallel: true and retries 0 locally, and e2e.log shows 'Running 218 tests using 4 workers'. Each claim checks out. Pause: manage-hours.spec.ts:16-18 pauses ordering for the whole cafe, and placeOrder reads it under its transaction, so any Order placed in the 1 to 3 seconds before Resume is refused, not only when the test dies. Busy Mode: the first Scheduled chip (bar.spec.ts:31-34) always starts before now + Prep Time + 15, so it gets 'window_unavailable' at place.ts:235-243 if Busy Mode starts between render and submit. e2e.log shows #110 Phase 2 (desktop, 39.4s) running across #114 Busy Mode (13.9s). Price: manage-menu.spec.ts:40 sets 170 and never restores it, so a save between the checkout render and submit gives price_changed. Queue: order-status.spec.ts:20-23 leaves an Order in 'preparing' in each project, so Prep Time goes from 5 to 10 mid-run. The roadmap's own 7.5 entry reports 'a different Staff test fails each run' and asks this review to fix the shared state, so the fit is strong.
verdicts.corrections: Sub-point (5) is overstated. The capacity_rules UPDATE writes the same values every time. Deleting checkout-ip, link-ip, second-factor and signup- keys breaks no test, because the 11th-try test is limited per Cart (checkout:${cartKey}) and no test asserts the link or Second Factor limits. Sub-point (6) is moot today: the repo has no .github/workflows, so retries: 2 never applies. Only the missing local trace (trace 'on-first-retry' with 0 retries) is real. refunds.spec.ts:30 moves an Order to picked_up, which does not count in the queue. Sub-point (1) is understated: the pause hurts other workers during the normal run, not only when the test dies.

verdicts.title: data/mail is never emptied: every sign-in rereads the whole outbox (1.2 s per pass at 1,267 files), and Vitest adds about 75 files per run to the same folder
verdicts.problem: Without a Resend key, every Vitest and e2e email is written to the developer's data/mail folder, and nothing ever empties it. linkFor reads every file on each poll of a sign-in, so sign-ins get slower with every run and old emails stay where assertions can match them.
verdicts.fix: Empty the outbox at the start of an e2e run (in reset-db.mts), or give e2e and Vitest their own MAIL_DIR. Have linkFor and checkout.spec read only files whose name ends with the address, as order-emails.test.ts:25-31 already does.
verdicts.reasoning: outbox.ts:52-63 writes to path.join(process.cwd(), 'data', 'mail') whenever RESEND_API_KEY is empty and VERCEL is unset. That holds for .env.test (the key is empty) and for the e2e webServer env, which sets no key. reset-db.mts only resets and seeds the database. linkFor (sign-in.ts:15-23) reads every file on each expect.poll attempt. signIn has 32 call sites, and qa:full runs Vitest and then Playwright one after the other, so emptying the folder at e2e start is safe. Today the folder holds 1,525 files (5.0 MB on disk), 1,118 of them stamped with the frozen Vitest time 2026-11-02T01-00-00-000Z, plus 2027-dated files from the clock-shift probes. My read-only scan (verify/tests-1/scan.mjs) took 538 to 666 ms per full pass. The 1.2 s figure was measured under load, and the cost grows linearly with the file count. The roadmap's 7.5 entry names exactly this ('data/mail is never emptied, so old sign-in emails pile up') as something the tests review should fix.
verdicts.corrections: signIn has 32 call sites in 11 files, not 10. A full pass took 0.54 to 0.67 s at 1,525 files on this check, not 1.2 s; the time depends on machine load. DATA-10 (production builds off Vercel keep emails on disk) is related, but it is a privacy problem, not the same one.

verdicts.title: checkout.spec's 'Order placed' email check (ORD-10) passes on old emails: Order Codes restart at K-001 every run
verdicts.problem: The e2e check for the 'Order placed' email searches every file in data/mail for 'Order K-0NN at Hoshikopi'. Order Codes restart each run and earlier runs left those subjects behind, so the check cannot fail on this machine.
verdicts.fix: Use a unique address such as hoshi-${Date.now()}@example.com and read only that address's files, or match the Order's own link (/orders/<id>?t=). Emptying the outbox per run (finding 5) also closes it.
verdicts.reasoning: checkout.spec.ts:37-46 reads all files and checks texts.some(t => t.includes(`Order ${code} at Hoshikopi`)). Today 'Order K-001 at Hoshikopi' appears in 617 files and there are 78 distinct codes, so whatever code this test gets is almost surely already present. The e2e assertion is dead. The impact is smaller than stated, though: emailOrderPlaced is called inside placeOrder (place.ts:321), and tests/db/order-emails.test.ts places an Order with a unique address and asserts the 'Order placed' email and its link. If the email stopped being sent, that DB test would fail. Only a failure specific to the production server (cwd or env) would slip through.
verdicts.corrections: Severity medium to low. ORD-10 is still covered by tests/db/order-emails.test.ts, which goes through the same placeOrder to emailOrderPlaced path with a unique address. The finding notes that test is sound, but its impact line ('if the Order placed email stopped being sent, this test would stay green') ignores that the suite as a whole would still catch it. The send call is at place.ts:319-322, not status.ts:191-204.

verdicts.title: The e2e suite depends on the Manila wall clock: one test fails from about 21:15 and nearly every ordering test from about 23:20, not only after 23:45 as db.ts says
verdicts.problem: The e2e server reads the real clock, and the test cafe's last Pickup Window starts at 23:30. So the chips test, which needs 9 windows, fails from about 21:20 Manila time, and ASAP placement fails from about 23:20, though db.ts says tests fail only from 23:45. Running npm run test:e2e or qa:full late in the evening gives red runs unrelated to the code.
verdicts.fix: Make the 8.3 chips test pick from what is offered and skip with a reason when fewer than 9 windows remain, and correct the db.ts comment. Optionally have reset-db.mts refuse to start between 21:00 and 00:30 Manila with a clear message.
verdicts.reasoning: openAllDayToday sets 00:00 to 23:59. pickupWindows (ordering-day.ts) offers windows while minute + 15 <= closes, so the last one starts at 23:30, and only windows starting at or after now + Prep Time are offered. checkout-form.tsx:44 has CHIPS = 6, and checkout.spec.ts:159 takes option nth(2) of Later today, so 9 windows are needed and the 9th from last starts at 21:30. With Prep Time 5 the test fails from 21:25, with 10 (two Preparing drinks left by order-status.spec) from 21:20, and with Busy Mode from about 21:05. ASAP gets no_window once now + Prep Time passes 23:30, from about 23:20 to 23:25. night-2350.log and future-0200.log show Vitest passing 228/228 with a shifted clock, so only e2e is affected. Impact is limited: the failure is predictable, confined to late evening, and avoided by running at another time, and there is no CI to run it at a bad hour.
verdicts.corrections: The thresholds start about 5 minutes later than stated: 21:20 to 21:25 with Prep Time 5 or 10, not 21:15. The 'scheduled CI run' impact is moot because there is no .github/workflows. Severity medium to low: the failure is deterministic and time-boxed, with a trivial workaround. The env-driven clock offset in the recommendation would add a time-shift knob to production builds (next start). Prefer the short-term test fix. The window loop is in ordering-day.ts:55-82, not 41-79.

Add two short placeOrder tests: a Reward with no drink in the Cart gives reward_unavailable, and an all-day cafe at 23:40 gives no_window.

verdicts.title: Concurrent adds to one Cart are still untested and still lose quantity; a first add racing another now also throws
verdicts.problem: addLine reads the Line's quantity, adds in JavaScript and upserts the result with no lock, so concurrent adds to one Cart overwrite each other. Two first adds for a new Cart can also race on the Cart's unique owner key and throw.
verdicts.fix: Write the failing test first: six concurrent addLine calls should give quantity 6 and no error. Then make the add atomic: an INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (cart_id, choice_key) DO UPDATE that increments quantity, capped at 20, or lock the Cart row with the existing lockCart before reading.
verdicts.reasoning: cart.ts:80-102 does cart.upsert, then cartLine.findUnique, computes quantity = existing + input, then cartLine.upsert with that absolute value, all without a transaction or lock. probe-matrix.log shows five '{"ok":true}', one rejected 'Invalid `client.cart.upsert()` invocation', and 'quantity [ 2 ]' after six adds. cart.test.ts has concurrency tests only for mergeGuestCart (line 151); 7.1 added lockCart to placeOrder and mergeGuestCart but not to addLine. Low severity fits: the Add button is disabled while pending, so it takes two tabs, the Pairing add beside the main add, or a retried request to hit it.

verdicts.title: Vitest takes 200 to 300 s: 42 s is one ESLint cold start, about 95 s is reseeding before every database test, and isolate: false would save only 12 to 17 s
locations: tests/db/*.test.ts beforeEach (resetDb + seedDatabase in 23 of 25 database files)
verdicts.problem: The unit run takes 3.5 to 5 minutes, and most of it is fixed setup: one ESLint cold start of about 42 s in module-boundary.test.ts and a TRUNCATE plus full reseed of about 0.6 s before each of about 145 database tests. That slows every local check and would slow a CI job.
verdicts.fix: Seed once per run and restore from a snapshot (or seed once per file in beforeAll where tests do not mutate shared rows), and lint the module-boundary rule with a minimal ESLint config instead of the full Next config. Leave isolate: false for later, since it saves only about 11 to 17 s.
verdicts.reasoning: Recomputed from the saved vitest-full.json with durations.cjs: module-boundary.test.ts 41.8 s for 3 tests (all in its first test), database files 0.73 to 1.8 s per test, pricing.test and seed.test (which seed once in beforeAll) 0.03 to 0.05 s per test, sum 179 s. 23 database files call resetDb plus seedDatabase in beforeEach; seedDatabase issues dozens of sequential creates and a findUnique+update loop for pairings. The gate run took 209 s and the saved full run 299 s; Vitest's own hints in the saved logs say 10.6 to 17 s for isolate: false. The snapshot idea is sound: the seed reads the wall clock (Date.now), not clock.ts, so a snapshot taken at global setup gives the same rows within one run.
verdicts.corrections: About 145 tests reseed per test (157 database tests minus pricing.test 8 and seed.test 4), not about 155; at about 0.63 s each that is about 90 s, close to the stated 95 s. helpers.ts:21-30 is only the TRUNCATE (about 60 ms); the 0.55 s seed call lives in each test file's beforeEach. The snapshot needs two variants or a post-restore delete, because 4 files seed with { people: false }. Linting only the exported rule object stops testing that eslint.config.mjs actually wires the rule in, a small loss. The isolate saving in today's gate log is 10.6 s, not 12.

verdicts.title: Smallest useful CI: one job with a Postgres service runs lint, format, typecheck, Vitest and audit in about 6 minutes; e2e stays manual or on a timed schedule
verdicts.problem: No .github folder exists, so pull requests merge into main with no automatic lint, typecheck or test run while Vercel deploys main to production and migrates its database. The quality gates run only when someone remembers npm run qa.
verdicts.fix: Add one GitHub Actions job on pull_request and push to main with a postgres:17 service and a hoshikopi_test database, then run npm ci, lint, format:check, typecheck, npx vitest run and npm audit --omit=dev, and require it on main. Keep Playwright manual or on a schedule until the shared-state and wall-clock e2e findings are fixed.
verdicts.reasoning: Checked that the proposal works with this repo: .env.test is git-ignored, and global-setup loads it with dotenv quiet:true, which does not throw when the file is missing; vitest.config's loadEnv('test', cwd, '') with an empty prefix copies process.env through, so job-level env is enough. helpers.ts requires a database name ending in _test, which hoshikopi_test meets. prisma.config.ts makes the datasource URL optional, so the postinstall prisma generate in npm ci works, and global-setup runs prisma migrate deploy with DIRECT_URL set. src/generated is git-ignored and is rebuilt by postinstall. No source code reads process.env.CI, and no date call depends on the machine time zone (no getHours, getDate or toLocale* without a zone), so a UTC runner is fine; the saved clock-shift probes (night-2350.log, future-0200.log) show Vitest passes at 23:50 and 02:00. Nothing in docs/adr records a decision against CI. Node 24 matches the local v24.18.0.
verdicts.corrections: This repeats ops:4 (same job, same steps) and should be merged with it; ID1-17 is about an outdated better-auth, which ops:4's Dependabot part covers, not this job. PAYMENT_PROVIDER and CRON_SECRET are not needed by Vitest (fake is already the default provider) but do no harm. npm audit --omit=dev fails on any new advisory at any level, which would turn unrelated PRs red; run it with --audit-level=high or as a separate check that is not required.

verdicts.title: MENU-04's e2e check waits up to 150 s, so it would still pass if updateTag('menu') were lost; Phase 1's exit says 'within seconds'
verdicts.problem: expectOnMenu reloads for up to 150 s and the Special Hours check for up to 75 s, while public reads use cacheLife('minutes') and refresh by themselves about a minute after any change. A save that never calls updateTag would still pass both checks.
verdicts.fix: Fail the check if the change is not visible within about 15 s (one stale visit allowed), or add an action-level test that asserts each menu and hours action calls updateTag with its tag. Fix or explain the slow refresh in staff:2 first, or the tighter check will be flaky.
verdicts.reasoning: getMenu is 'use cache' with cacheTag('menu') and cacheLife('minutes'), so an entry older than 60 s is served stale once and refilled. The e2e server builds right before the run, so by the time a menu test saves, the cached entries are usually already over a minute old, and a missing updateTag would show the change on the second or third reload, well inside 150 s. verdicts.title: The e2e server inherits .env.local for every variable playwright.config.ts does not set, and builds into the same .next folder as any local production server
verdicts.problem: The Playwright web server sets only seven variables, so next build and next start take RESEND_API_KEY, MAIL_FROM, Google and Blob settings from the developer's .env.local. It also builds into the default .next folder, so e2e cannot run beside an ad-hoc local production server on port 3300 or 3400.
verdicts.fix: Set RESEND_API_KEY, GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID, GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET, BLOB_STORE_ID and BLOB_READ_WRITE_TOKEN to empty strings in webServer.env so e2e is hermetic. If e2e must run beside another production server, read distDir from an env var and also add the new folder to .gitignore, .prettierignore and the ESLint global ignores.
verdicts.reasoning: Playwright merges webServer.env over process.env, and Next loads .env.local for build and start without overriding variables already set, so every unset key comes from .env.local. Today .env.local has RESEND_API_KEY, Google and Blob keys empty and MAIL_FROM set (checked key presence only), so nothing breaks yet; it is a latent trap. next.config.ts sets no distDir. docs/08-TOOLING.md section 3 reserves 3300 and 3400 for ad-hoc production servers, which share .next; npm run dev is unaffected because Next 16 builds dev into .next/dev.
verdicts.corrections: The impact is overstated. outbox.ts:17-18 never sends @hoshikopi.example addresses to Resend, so Staff sign-ins (Christian, Annika, Hoshi and the e2e-*@hoshikopi.example Barista) keep using data/mail; only tests with @example.com addresses would break (Member sign-ins in members, privacy, stars and manage role specs, the Event Sign-up, and checkout's email check). 'Test addresses are emailed for real' is also overstated: example.com is a reserved domain, and with the default onboarding@resend.dev sender Resend refuses non-owner recipients, so sends fail instead of delivering. A custom distDir is linted by ESLint (globalIgnores covers only .next/**) and is not git-ignored, so the second fix needs those ignores too.
